# Key figures

The three subsections below show the central figures of the analysis up front, so that readers do not need to page through ~3,000 lines of analytical code to see the results. The figures are embedded from pre-rendered PNGs that the analytical workflow below produces on each knit; the code that generates them lives in sections 10 (continuous scale-of-effect profiles) and 11 (domain bar charts, under *Summary Tables*). If the PNGs do not yet exist (e.g. on a fresh clone of the repository where the figures have not been committed), each subsection will render a placeholder message.

## Scale-of-effect profiles by covariate

Each of the seven panels below shows the estimated coefficient (log-rate scale) for one habitat covariate as a function of buffer radius, with separate curves per species × month (horse monthly; cattle bimonthly; elk quarterly). Ribbons are 95 % CIs from the fitted multivariate NB GLMMs; non-zero domains are the contiguous buffer ranges where the 95 % CI excludes zero. Multivariate models are shown of the left, univariate on the right. See Section 10 for the code that produces these.

```{r key-fig-scale-of-effect, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.align="center"}

    "scale_of_effect_p_shrub.png",

)

}
```

## Domain bar chart — multivariate models (Figure 2 in manuscript)

The domain bar chart summarises every scale-of-effect profile as a set of coloured segments: blue segments mark contiguous buffer ranges with a positive non-zero domain (95 % CI > 0 throughout), red segments mark negative domains, and unmarked ranges indicate CI-crossing zero. Filled diamonds mark the scale of effect within each domain (largest |β|); filled stars mark the global peak across a species × period × covariate profile. Brackets connect same-sign split domains whose peak-scale CIs overlap, indicating statistical indistinguishability in effect magnitude. See §11.4 for code.

```{r key-fig-domain-bars-mv, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.align="center"}
domain_mv_path <- file.path(fig_dir, "domain_bar_chart.png")
if (file.exists(domain_mv_path)) {
  knitr::include_graphics(domain_mv_path)
} else {
  cat("*Multivariate domain bar chart not yet generated. Knit the full document once; the figure will be embedded on subsequent renders.*")
}
```

## Domain bar chart — univariate models (SI sensitivity analysis)

To provide exploratory monthly-resolution information on scale of effect dynamics for all three species, we fitted univariate models for each predictor at each spatial extent and month. These models included only a single habitat predictor plus the SAC, effort offset, and strata random effect. For herbaceous NDVI, we fitted bivariate models pairing herbaceous NDVI with proportion herbaceous to maintain interpretability. Monthly univariate models were fitted for horses (May–October), cattle (July–October), and elk (May–October). Univariate models do not control for other landscape predictors and therefore may reflect confounded associations. These results are presented as exploratory context for interpreting temporal dynamics and should not be used for direct inference about habitat associations. To assess agreement between univariate and multivariate inferences, we compared the two analyses for horses (the only species with matching temporal resolution) at both the profile level (sign, peak scale, and 95% CI overlap at the global peak) and the buffer-cell level (sign classification across 672 cells). 

The univariate domain bar chart repeats the domain-based summary but using single-covariate models (each habitat covariate fit alone with only the spatial autocovariate and stratum random intercept retained). The domain bar chart summarises every scale-of-effect profile as a set of coloured segments: blue segments mark contiguous buffer ranges with a positive non-zero domain (95 % CI > 0 throughout), red segments mark negative domains, and unmarked ranges indicate CI-crossing zero. Filled diamonds mark the scale of effect within each domain (largest absolute effect size); filled stars mark the global peak across a species × period × covariate profile. Brackets connect same-sign split domains whose peak-scale CIs overlap, indicating statistical indistinguishability in effect magnitude. 

This tests which scale-of-effect features are driven by the covariate itself versus its co-conditioning on other covariates in the multivariate model. All three species are shown at monthly resolution. See §11.7 for the formal univariate-vs-multivariate agreement analysis (horse).

In evaluating the agreement between multivariate (MV) and univariate (UV) models for horses (the 42 horse profiles with matched temporal structure (6 months × 7 predictors)) the UV analysis reproduced the MV domain sign in 25 of 30 profiles (83%). UV models produced 13% more domains overall (51 vs. 45 in MV models). UV scale of effect within each of the 45 domains that MV models also detected agreed 38% of the time (49% within ±1 buffer), and global peak scales of effect agreed 39% of the time (46% within ±1 buffer). Cell-level agreement across all 672 buffers (6 months * 7 predictors * 16 buffers) agreed on sign 77% of the time. The 23% disagreement was only between null and signed domains; there were no sign reversals (§ 11.7). 

```{r key-fig-domain-bars-uni, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.align="center"}

if (file.exists(domain_uni_path)) {
  knitr::include_graphics(domain_uni_path)
} else {
  cat("*Univariate domain bar chart not yet generated. Knit the full document once; the figure will be embedded on subsequent renders.*")
}
```

# Data Preparation

## Load and inspect

```{r load-data}
dat_raw <- read_csv(data_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

cat("Rows:", nrow(dat_raw), "\n")
cat("Species:", unique(dat_raw$species), "\n")
cat("Months:", sort(unique(dat_raw$month)), "\n")
cat("Scales:", sort(unique(dat_raw$extent_radius_m)), "\n")
cat("N scales:", n_distinct(dat_raw$extent_radius_m), "\n")
```

## Define constants

```{r constants}
# Spatial scales (16 radii)
all_scales <- sort(unique(dat_raw$extent_radius_m))

# All habitat covariates (7 total)
habitat_covars <- c("p_herb", "NDVI_herb", "p_shrub", "p_harvest",
                     "p_wetland", "hu", "tri")

# Covariates eligible for dredging (6 total — NDVI_herb excluded).
# NDVI_herb cannot be dredged because it contains structural NAs where
# p_herb = 0, and it must always appear with p_herb in the model to
# ensure the imputed zeros are interpretable. NDVI_herb is handled
# exclusively through the substitution procedure (see below).
dredge_covars <- c("p_herb", "p_shrub", "p_harvest", "p_wetland", "hu", "tri")

# Species-specific covariate budgets (environmental covariates only;
# SAC, offset, and strata random effect are always included on top of these)
covar_budget <- list(
  Horse  = 5,
  Cattle = 4,
  Elk    = 2
)

# Temporal structures
horse_months  <- 5:10                       # May-Oct monthly
cattle_bimonthly <- list(                   # Two bimonthly periods
  "Jul-Aug"  = c(7, 8),
  "Sep-Oct"  = c(9, 10)
)
cattle_univar_months <- 7:10                # Jul-Oct for univariate
elk_quarterly <- list(                      # Two quarterly periods
  "May-Jul" = c(5, 6, 7),
  "Aug-Oct" = c(8, 9, 10)
)
elk_univar_months  <- 5:10                  # May-Oct for univariate
horse_univar_months <- 5:10                 # May-Oct for univariate
```

## Prepare analysis datasets

### Impute NDVI_herb NAs and exclude HU NAs

```{r prep-data}
# Drop rows where hu is NA FIRST (edge locations outside IDW interpolation extent)
# This ensures consistent sample sizes across all downstream analyses.
n_before_hu <- nrow(dat_raw)
dat <- dat_raw %>% filter(!is.na(hu))
cat("Dropped", n_before_hu - nrow(dat), "rows with NA hu values\n")

# Impute NDVI_herb NA to 0
# Rationale: NA occurs where p_herb = 0 (no herbaceous pixels in buffer).
# Setting to 0 conflates "no habitat" with "lowest greenness", but p_herb
# in the same model captures habitat availability independently.
# This artifact is most pronounced at fine scales.
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(NDVI_herb = replace_na(NDVI_herb, 0))

cat("Remaining rows:", nrow(dat), "\n")

# Verify no remaining NAs in covariates (QA check; suppressed in SI)
covar_na_check <- dat %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(habitat_covars), ~sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "covariate", values_to = "n_na")
invisible(covar_na_check)
```

### Compute spatial autocovariate (SAC)

The SAC accounts for spatial autocorrelation in detection counts. It is computed
as the inverse-distance-weighted mean of detection rates at neighbouring cameras
within a 20 km bandwidth, determined from the semivariogram range (Stage 1 EDA).

```{r compute-sac}
compute_sac <- function(data, bandwidth_km = 20) {
  # Compute SAC using inverse-distance-weighted mean of neighbours'
  # detection rates within a fixed bandwidth.
  # data must be at the location level (one scale only)

  n <- nrow(data)
  if (n < 2) return(rep(NA_real_, n))

  coords <- as.matrix(data[, c("longitude", "latitude")])
  det_rate <- data$n_det / data$camera_days

  # Distance matrix in km (approximate using Euclidean on decimal degrees)
  # For Alberta foothills (~51°N), 1° lat ≈ 111 km, 1° lon ≈ 70 km
  lat_km <- coords[, 2] * 111.32
  lon_km <- coords[, 1] * 111.32 * cos(mean(coords[, 2]) * pi / 180)
  coords_km <- cbind(lon_km, lat_km)
  dist_km <- as.matrix(dist(coords_km))

  # IDW within bandwidth: weight = 1/distance, zero weight beyond bandwidth
  sac_values <- numeric(n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    neighbours <- which(dist_km[i, ] > 0 & dist_km[i, ] <= bandwidth_km)
    if (length(neighbours) == 0) {
      sac_values[i] <- NA_real_
    } else {
      weights <- 1 / dist_km[i, neighbours]
      sac_values[i] <- sum(weights * det_rate[neighbours]) / sum(weights)
    }
  }

  return(sac_values)
}

# Compute SAC at the reference scale (location-level; scale doesn't affect coords)
ref_scale <- all_scales[1]

sac_df <- dat %>%
  filter(extent_radius_m == ref_scale) %>%
  group_by(species, year, month) %>%
  mutate(sac = compute_sac(pick(everything()), bandwidth_km = 20)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(location, species, year, month, sac)

# Join SAC back to all scales
dat <- dat %>%
  left_join(sac_df, by = c("location", "species", "year", "month"))

cat("SAC NAs:", sum(is.na(dat$sac)), "\n")
# SAC per-species range summary suppressed in SI (operational diagnostic only;
# SAC performance is assessed formally in S6: SAC sensitivity analysis).
```

### Create pooled datasets

```{r pooled-datasets}
# Function to pool months: sum n_det and camera_days, mean for time-varying covars
pool_months <- function(data, month_vec, period_label) {
  data %>%
    filter(month %in% month_vec) %>%
    group_by(location, species, year, extent_radius_m, strata, strata_code,
             latitude, longitude) %>%
    summarise(
      n_det = sum(n_det),
      camera_days = sum(camera_days),
      # Static covariates: take first (identical across months)
      p_herb = first(p_herb),
      p_shrub = first(p_shrub),
      p_wetland = first(p_wetland),
      p_harvest = first(p_harvest),
      tri = first(tri),
      # Time-varying covariates: mean across pooled months
      NDVI_herb = mean(NDVI_herb, na.rm = TRUE),
      hu = mean(hu, na.rm = TRUE),
      # SAC: mean across pooled months
      sac = mean(sac, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      log_effort = log(camera_days),
      period = period_label
    ) %>%
    # Drop locations with < 7 total camera days in pooled period
    filter(camera_days >= 7)
}

# Cattle bimonthly datasets
cattle_bimonthly_data <- map2_dfr(
  cattle_bimonthly,
  names(cattle_bimonthly),
  ~ pool_months(filter(dat, species == "Cattle"), .x, .y)
)

# Elk quarterly datasets (May-Jul, Aug-Oct)
elk_quarterly_data <- map2_dfr(
  elk_quarterly,
  names(elk_quarterly),
  ~ pool_months(filter(dat, species == "Elk"), .x, .y)
)

# Quick summary suppressed in SI — operational diagnostic only.
# Sample sizes and zero-inflation rates are reported in the main text and
# Table 1 caption; running totals during pooling are not reader-facing.
```

# Model Fitting Functions

## Core model fitting

```{r model-functions}
# Fit a single NB GLMM with specified covariates at a given scale
fit_nb_glmm <- function(data, covars, scale_m, standardize = TRUE) {
  # Filter to the target scale
  d <- data %>% filter(extent_radius_m == scale_m)

  if (nrow(d) < 10) return(NULL)

  # Standardize covariates (including SAC)
  vars_to_scale <- c(covars, "sac")
  for (v in vars_to_scale) {
    if (v %in% names(d)) {
      d[[v]] <- as.numeric(scale(d[[v]]))
    }
  }

  # Build formula: n_det ~ covars + sac + offset(log_effort) + (1|strata)
  fixed_terms <- paste(c(covars, "sac"), collapse = " + ")
  form <- as.formula(
    paste0("n_det ~ ", fixed_terms, " + offset(log_effort) + (1|strata)")
  )

  # Fit with glmmTMB
  tryCatch({
    mod <- glmmTMB(form, data = d, family = nbinom2)

    # Check convergence
    if (!mod$sdr$pdHess) {
      warning("Non-positive-definite Hessian at scale ", scale_m)
    }

    return(mod)
  }, error = function(e) {
    warning("Model failed at scale ", scale_m, ": ", e$message)
    return(NULL)
  })
}


# Fit a univariate NB GLMM (single habitat covariate + SAC)
fit_univariate <- function(data, covar, scale_m) {
  fit_nb_glmm(data, covars = covar, scale_m = scale_m)
}


# Extract tidy results from a fitted model
tidy_model <- function(mod, species, period, scale_m, model_type, covars_in_model) {
  if (is.null(mod)) {
    return(tibble(
      species = species, period = period, extent_radius_m = scale_m,
      model_type = model_type, covars_in_model = paste(covars_in_model, collapse = "+"),
      term = NA_character_, estimate = NA_real_, std.error = NA_real_,
      statistic = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_, converged = FALSE, AIC = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  tryCatch({
    tidy_out <- broom.mixed::tidy(mod, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE)
    tidy_out %>%
      mutate(
        species = species,
        period = period,
        extent_radius_m = scale_m,
        model_type = model_type,
        covars_in_model = paste(covars_in_model, collapse = "+"),
        converged = mod$sdr$pdHess,
        AIC = AIC(mod)
      )
  }, error = function(e) {
    tibble(
      species = species, period = period, extent_radius_m = scale_m,
      model_type = model_type, covars_in_model = paste(covars_in_model, collapse = "+"),
      term = NA_character_, estimate = NA_real_, std.error = NA_real_,
      statistic = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_, converged = FALSE, AIC = NA_real_
    )
  })
}
```

## DHARMa diagnostics

```{r dharma-functions}
# Run DHARMa tests on a single model, return summary row
dharma_check <- function(mod, species, period, scale_m, model_type) {
  if (is.null(mod)) {
    return(tibble(
      species = species, period = period, extent_radius_m = scale_m,
      model_type = model_type,
      uniformity_p = NA_real_, dispersion_p = NA_real_, outlier_p = NA_real_,
      flag = NA
    ))
  }

  tryCatch({
    sim <- simulateResiduals(mod, n = 500, plot = FALSE)
    unif <- testUniformity(sim, plot = FALSE)
    disp <- testDispersion(sim, plot = FALSE)
    outl <- testOutliers(sim, plot = FALSE)

    tibble(
      species = species, period = period, extent_radius_m = scale_m,
      model_type = model_type,
      uniformity_p = unif$p.value,
      dispersion_p = disp$p.value,
      outlier_p = outl$p.value,
      # Flag at alpha = 0.01 to account for multiple testing
      flag = uniformity_p < 0.01 | dispersion_p < 0.01 | outlier_p < 0.01
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    tibble(
      species = species, period = period, extent_radius_m = scale_m,
      model_type = model_type,
      uniformity_p = NA_real_, dispersion_p = NA_real_, outlier_p = NA_real_,
      flag = NA
    )
  })
}
```

# AIC-based Covariate Selection

## Dredge function

For each species-period, fit all combinations of the specified size from the 6
dredge-eligible habitat covariates (always including SAC + strata + offset).
Do this at each of 16 scales. Compute AIC weights within each scale, then sum
variable importance across scales. Select the top-k covariates.

NDVI_herb is excluded from the dredge because it contains structural NAs (when
p_herb = 0) and must always co-occur with p_herb in any model. It is handled
exclusively through the substitution procedure.

```{r dredge-function}
# Fit all covariate combinations of size k at one scale, return AIC table
dredge_at_scale <- function(data, k, scale_m, covars_to_dredge) {
  combos <- combn(covars_to_dredge, k, simplify = FALSE)

  results <- map_dfr(combos, function(covars) {
    mod <- fit_nb_glmm(data, covars, scale_m)
    if (is.null(mod)) {
      return(tibble(
        covars = paste(sort(covars), collapse = "+"),
        AIC = NA_real_,
        extent_radius_m = scale_m
      ))
    }
    tibble(
      covars = paste(sort(covars), collapse = "+"),
      AIC = AIC(mod),
      extent_radius_m = scale_m
    )
  })

  # Compute delta AIC and AIC weights within this scale
  results <- results %>%
    filter(!is.na(AIC)) %>%
    mutate(
      delta_AIC = AIC - min(AIC),
      aic_weight = exp(-0.5 * delta_AIC) / sum(exp(-0.5 * delta_AIC))
    )

  return(results)
}


# Compute variable importance: sum of AIC weights for models containing each covariate.
# Uses exact string matching on split covariate names to avoid substring false positives.
compute_variable_importance <- function(dredge_results, covars_to_dredge) {
  importance <- map_dfr(covars_to_dredge, function(cv) {
    # Robust membership check: split on "+" and test exact match
    containing <- dredge_results %>%
      filter(map_lgl(covars, ~ cv %in% str_split(.x, "\\+")[[1]]))

    tibble(
      covariate = cv,
      cumulative_aic_weight = sum(containing$aic_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_top_model = sum(containing$delta_AIC == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_models = nrow(containing)
    )
  }) %>%
    arrange(desc(cumulative_aic_weight))

  return(importance)
}
```

# Horse Analysis

## Covariate selection

```{r horse-select, cache=TRUE}
horse_data <- dat %>% filter(species == "Horse")

# Dredge within each month × scale combination using the 6 dredge-eligible
# covariates, then aggregate variable importance across all month-scale cells.
cat("=== Dredging: Horse | Monthly × 16 scales ===\n")
cat(sprintf("  %d combinations × %d months × %d scales = %d models\n",
            choose(length(dredge_covars), covar_budget$Horse),
            length(horse_months), length(all_scales),
            choose(length(dredge_covars), covar_budget$Horse) *
              length(horse_months) * length(all_scales)))

horse_dredge_grid <- expand_grid(month = horse_months, scale = all_scales)

horse_dredge_all <- future_pmap_dfr(horse_dredge_grid, function(month, scale) {
  d <- horse_data %>% filter(month == !!month)
  res <- dredge_at_scale(d, covar_budget$Horse, scale, dredge_covars)
  res %>% mutate(month = month)
}, .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE), .progress = TRUE)

horse_importance <- compute_variable_importance(horse_dredge_all, dredge_covars)
# Variable-importance rankings are reported formally in Table 1 (§11.1);
# intermediate printout suppressed here.

# Select top 5 covariates (base model set)
horse_top5 <- horse_importance$covariate[1:covar_budget$Horse]

# Weakest base covariate = rank 5 (last to make the AIC cut).
# Fixed across all months for consistent conditioning sets.
horse_weakest <- horse_importance$covariate[covar_budget$Horse]

# Second-weakest = rank 4 (needed if p_herb not in base for NDVI substitution)
horse_second_weakest <- horse_importance$covariate[covar_budget$Horse - 1]

# Non-NDVI substitution covariates (from the 6 dredge candidates, those not in base)
horse_substituted <- setdiff(dredge_covars, horse_top5)

cat("\nHorse base covariates:", paste(horse_top5, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Horse weakest (to be dropped for substitution):", horse_weakest, "\n")
cat("Horse second-weakest (for NDVI + p_herb forcing):", horse_second_weakest, "\n")
cat("Horse non-NDVI substitution covariates:", paste(horse_substituted, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("p_herb in base model:", "p_herb" %in% horse_top5, "\n")

horse_selection <- list(
  top_covars = horse_top5,
  importance = horse_importance,
  dredge_results = horse_dredge_all
)
```

## Base models (5 covariates × 6 months × 16 scales)

```{r horse-base, cache=TRUE}
horse_grid <- expand_grid(
  month = horse_months,
  extent_radius_m = all_scales
)

horse_base_results <- future_pmap_dfr(horse_grid, function(month, extent_radius_m) {
  d <- horse_data %>% filter(month == !!month)
  mod <- fit_nb_glmm(d, horse_top5, extent_radius_m)
  tidy_model(mod, "Horse", month.abb[month], extent_radius_m,
             "base", horse_top5)
}, .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE), .progress = TRUE)

cat("Horse base models fitted:", nrow(horse_grid), "\n")
cat("Converged:",
    horse_base_results %>%
      distinct(period, extent_radius_m, converged) %>%
      pull(converged) %>% sum(na.rm = TRUE),
    "of", nrow(horse_grid), "\n")
```

## Substitution models (non-NDVI)

For each month × scale, drop the weakest covariate (fixed across all months)
from the base 5 and substitute in each excluded non-NDVI covariate one at a time.

```{r horse-substitution, cache=TRUE}
cat("Horse weakest covariate (fixed across months):", horse_weakest, "\n")

horse_sub_grid <- expand_grid(
  month = horse_months,
  extent_radius_m = all_scales,
  sub_covar = horse_substituted
)

horse_sub_results <- future_pmap_dfr(horse_sub_grid, function(month, extent_radius_m, sub_covar) {
  period_label <- month.abb[month]

  # Replace the weakest with the substituted covariate
  covars_sub <- c(setdiff(horse_top5, horse_weakest), sub_covar)

  d <- horse_data %>% filter(month == !!month)
  mod <- fit_nb_glmm(d, covars_sub, extent_radius_m)
  tidy_model(mod, "Horse", period_label, extent_radius_m,
             paste0("substitution_", sub_covar), covars_sub)
}, .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE), .progress = TRUE)

cat("Horse non-NDVI substitution models fitted:", nrow(horse_sub_grid), "\n")
```

## NDVI substitution models

NDVI_herb requires special handling: it must co-occur with p_herb in the model.
- If p_herb IS in the base set: drop the weakest, substitute NDVI_herb.
- If p_herb is NOT in the base set: drop the weakest for NDVI_herb AND the
  second-weakest for p_herb (forcing p_herb in). Model size stays at 5.

```{r horse-ndvi-substitution, cache=TRUE}
# Determine NDVI substitution covariate set
if ("p_herb" %in% horse_top5) {
  # p_herb already present — just swap weakest for NDVI_herb
  horse_ndvi_covars <- c(setdiff(horse_top5, horse_weakest), "NDVI_herb")
  cat("NDVI substitution (p_herb in base): dropping", horse_weakest,
      "for NDVI_herb\n")
} else {
  # p_herb absent — swap weakest for NDVI_herb AND second-weakest for p_herb
  horse_ndvi_covars <- c(
    setdiff(horse_top5, c(horse_weakest, horse_second_weakest)),
    "NDVI_herb", "p_herb"
  )
  cat("NDVI substitution (p_herb forced): dropping", horse_weakest,
      "for NDVI_herb and", horse_second_weakest, "for p_herb\n")
}
cat("NDVI model covariates:", paste(horse_ndvi_covars, collapse = ", "), "\n")

horse_ndvi_grid <- expand_grid(
  month = horse_months,
  extent_radius_m = all_scales
)

horse_ndvi_results <- future_pmap_dfr(horse_ndvi_grid, function(month, extent_radius_m) {
  period_label <- month.abb[month]
  d <- horse_data %>% filter(month == !!month)
  mod <- fit_nb_glmm(d, horse_ndvi_covars, extent_radius_m)
  tidy_model(mod, "Horse", period_label, extent_radius_m,
             "substitution_NDVI_herb", horse_ndvi_covars)
}, .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE), .progress = TRUE)

cat("Horse NDVI substitution models fitted:", nrow(horse_ndvi_grid), "\n")
```

## Univariate monthly models (May-Oct)

Univariate models for each non-NDVI covariate, plus bivariate models for
NDVI_herb (paired with p_herb to maintain interpretability).


```{r elk-select, cache=TRUE}
cat("=== Dredging: Elk | 2 quarterly periods × 16 scales ===\n")
cat(sprintf("  %d combinations × %d periods × %d scales = %d models\n",
            choose(length(dredge_covars), covar_budget$Elk),
            length(elk_quarterly), length(all_scales),
            choose(length(dredge_covars), covar_budget$Elk) *
              length(elk_quarterly) * length(all_scales)))

elk_dredge_grid <- expand_grid(
  period = names(elk_quarterly),
  scale = all_scales
)

elk_dredge_all <- future_pmap_dfr(elk_dredge_grid, function(period, scale) {
  d <- elk_quarterly_data %>% filter(period == !!period)
  dredge_at_scale(d, covar_budget$Elk, scale, dredge_covars) %>%
    mutate(period = period)
}, .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE), .progress = TRUE)

elk_importance <- compute_variable_importance(elk_dredge_all, dredge_covars)
# Variable-importance rankings are reported formally in Table 1 (§11.1);
# intermediate printout suppressed here.

elk_top2 <- elk_importance$covariate[1:covar_budget$Elk]
elk_weakest <- elk_importance$covariate[covar_budget$Elk]
# For elk (budget = 2), second-weakest = rank 1.
# If p_herb not in base, forcing both NDVI + p_herb replaces the ENTIRE base.
elk_second_weakest <- elk_importance$covariate[covar_budget$Elk - 1]
elk_substituted <- setdiff(dredge_covars, elk_top2)

cat("\nElk base covariates:", paste(elk_top2, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Elk weakest:", elk_weakest, "\n")
cat("Elk second-weakest:", elk_second_weakest, "\n")
cat("Elk non-NDVI substitution covariates:", paste(elk_substituted, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("p_herb in base model:", "p_herb" %in% elk_top2, "\n")

# NOTE: With budget = 2, if p_herb is NOT in the base model and NDVI
# must be paired with p_herb, the NDVI substitution replaces BOTH base
# covariates. This means the NDVI estimate has no shared conditioning
# covariates with the base model — interpret with caution and compare
# to the bivariate NDVI univariate estimate.

elk_selection <- list(
  top_covars = elk_top2,
  importance = elk_importance,
  dredge_results = elk_dredge_all
)
```

# DHARMa Diagnostics

Run DHARMa on all models and create a summary table with flagging.

**Note:** This section re-fits every model and runs 500 simulations each. For ~2000+
models this can take several hours. Set `dharma_subset` to TRUE below to run on a
representative subset (base models only) for faster iteration. Run the full set for
final reporting.

```{r dharma-all, cache=TRUE}
# Set to FALSE for full diagnostic run on all models
dharma_subset <- FALSE

# Re-fit and test a model given the row info from results
run_dharma_batch <- function(results_df, species_label, monthly_data,
                             pooled_data = NULL) {
  # Get unique model specifications
  model_specs <- results_df %>%
    distinct(period, extent_radius_m, model_type, covars_in_model) %>%
    filter(!is.na(covars_in_model))

  cat(sprintf("Running DHARMa for %s: %d models\n", species_label, nrow(model_specs)))

  future_pmap_dfr(model_specs, function(period, extent_radius_m, model_type, covars_in_model) {
    covars <- str_split(covars_in_model, "\\+")[[1]]

    # Determine which data to use based on period label
    is_monthly <- period %in% month.abb
    if (is_monthly) {
      month_num <- match(period, month.abb)
      d <- monthly_data %>% filter(month == month_num)
    } else if (!is.null(pooled_data)) {
      d <- pooled_data %>% filter(period == !!period)
    } else {
      return(dharma_check(NULL, species_label, period, extent_radius_m, model_type))
    }

    mod <- fit_nb_glmm(d, covars, extent_radius_m)
    dharma_check(mod, species_label, period, extent_radius_m, model_type)
  }, .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE), .progress = TRUE)
}

# Filter function for subsetting
filter_for_dharma <- function(results) {
  if (dharma_subset) {
    results %>% filter(model_type %in% c("base"))
  } else {
    results
  }
}

# Run DHARMa for each species
dharma_horse <- run_dharma_batch(
  filter_for_dharma(horse_all_results), "Horse",
  monthly_data = horse_data
)

dharma_cattle <- run_dharma_batch(
  filter_for_dharma(cattle_all_results), "Cattle",
  monthly_data = dat %>% filter(species == "Cattle"),
  pooled_data = cattle_bimonthly_data
)

dharma_elk <- run_dharma_batch(
  filter_for_dharma(elk_all_results), "Elk",
  monthly_data = dat %>% filter(species == "Elk"),
  pooled_data = elk_quarterly_data
)

dharma_all <- bind_rows(dharma_horse, dharma_cattle, dharma_elk)

# Disabled for JAE submission — diagnostic dump, not used by S1–S6 or Dryad.
# write_csv(dharma_all, file.path(output_dir, "dharma_diagnostics.csv"))
```

## DHARMa summary

```{r dharma-summary}
dharma_summary <- dharma_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(flag)) %>%
  group_by(species, model_type) %>%
  summarise(
    n_models = n(),
    pct_uniformity_fail = round(100 * mean(uniformity_p < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    pct_dispersion_fail = round(100 * mean(dispersion_p < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    pct_outlier_fail    = round(100 * mean(outlier_p < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    pct_any_fail        = round(100 * mean(flag, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(dharma_summary,
             caption = "DHARMa diagnostic failure rates (alpha = 0.01) by species and model type")

flagged <- dharma_all %>%
  filter(flag == TRUE) %>%
  arrange(species, period, extent_radius_m)

cat("\nFlagged models:", nrow(flagged), "of", nrow(dharma_all), "\n")

# Per-species / per-model-type breakdown of flagged models is captured in
# the DHARMa summary kable above and in the exported CSV. Intermediate
# printout suppressed in SI.
```

```{r assemble-results}
# write_csv(all_results, file.path(output_dir, "all_model_results.csv"))

# Create a clean plotting dataset: one row per species x period x scale x covariate
# For base models: keep all habitat covariate coefficients
# For substitution models: keep ONLY the substituted covariate's coefficient
# For univariate/bivariate models: keep the focal covariate only

plot_data <- all_results %>%
  filter(
    term != "(Intercept)",
    term != "sac",
    !is.na(estimate),
    converged
  ) %>%
  mutate(covariate = term)

# For substitution models, identify the TARGET covariate of each substitution.
# model_type encodes this as "substitution_<covariate_name>".
# This prevents the bug where a covariate appearing as a companion in a
# different substitution model (e.g., p_herb forced into the NDVI substitution)
# produces a duplicate coefficient in the plotting data.
plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  mutate(
    is_sub_target = case_when(
      covar_source == "substituted" &
        model_type == paste0("substitution_", covariate) ~ TRUE,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, extent_radius_m, covariate, covar_source,
         is_sub_target, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high,
         p.value, model_type)

# Filter logic:
# - From base models: keep all covariate coefficients
# - From substitution models: keep ONLY the target covariate of that substitution
#   (not companion covariates like p_herb forced in for NDVI models)
# - From univariate models: keep the single covariate
# - From bivariate_NDVI models (tagged as "univariate"): keep only NDVI_herb
plot_data_clean <- plot_data %>%
  filter(
    (covar_source == "base") |
    (covar_source == "substituted" & is_sub_target) |
    (covar_source == "univariate" & model_type == "univariate") |
    (covar_source == "univariate" & model_type == "bivariate_NDVI" &
       covariate == "NDVI_herb")
  )

# Disabled for JAE submission — not read by S1–S6 or included in Dryad.
# write_csv(plot_data_clean, file.path(output_dir, "plot_ready_results.csv"))

cat("Plot-ready results:", nrow(plot_data_clean), "rows\n")
cat("Covariates represented:", paste(unique(plot_data_clean$covariate), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r investigate-flagged}
# ── SI-trimmed flagged-model audit ──
# The full version of this chunk (see 02_multiscale_analysis_CI.Rmd in the
# project root) refits every flagged / implausible model and prints a
# DHARMa diagnostic panel for each. That output is an internal QA artefact
# — not a reader-facing result — so the SI reports only the aggregate
# counts, exports the suspect-model list as a CSV for reproducibility, and
# then applies the |β| > 10 cleanup.

# ---- 1. Models with implausible estimates (|β| on log-rate scale > 10) ----
implausible <- plot_data_clean %>%
  filter(abs(estimate) > 10) %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, extent_radius_m, covariate, covar_source,
                estimate, std.error, p.value)

# ---- 2. Unique suspect models (implausible ∪ DHARMa-flagged) ----
suspect_models <- bind_rows(
  implausible %>%
    distinct(species, period, extent_radius_m, covar_source) %>%
    mutate(reason = "implausible_estimate"),
  flagged %>%
    distinct(species, period, extent_radius_m, model_type) %>%
    rename(covar_source = model_type) %>%
    mutate(reason = "dharma_flag")
) %>%
  distinct(species, period, extent_radius_m, .keep_all = TRUE)

# ---- 3. Aggregate audit output ----
cat(sprintf(
  "Flagged-model audit:\n  Implausible estimates (|β| > 10): %d rows\n  DHARMa-flagged models:            %d rows\n  Unique suspect models (union):    %d rows\n",
  nrow(implausible), nrow(flagged), nrow(suspect_models)
))

# ---- 4. Export the suspect-model list ----
# Disabled for JAE submission — diagnostic dump, not used by S1–S6 or Dryad.
# write_csv(suspect_models,
#           file.path(output_dir, "dharma_suspect_models.csv"))

# ---- 5. Drop implausible-β rows from plot data ----
n_before <- nrow(plot_data_clean)
plot_data_clean <- plot_data_clean %>% filter(abs(estimate) <= 10)
cat(sprintf("Cleanup: removed %d rows with |β| > 10 from plot_data_clean.\n",
            n_before - nrow(plot_data_clean)))
```

## Plotting setup

```{r plot-setup, cache=FALSE}

# Month palette — strong contrast
month_pal <- c(
  "May" = "#FDBF6F",
  "Jun" = "#FF7F00",
  "Jul" = "#E31A1C",
  "Aug" = "#6A3D9A",
  "Sep" = "#1F78B4",

)

# Publication-quality covariate labels
covar_labels <- c(
  "p_herb"    = "Proportion herbaceous land cover",
  "NDVI_herb" = "Herbaceous NDVI (mean)*",
  "p_shrub"   = "Proportion shrub land cover",
  "p_harvest" = "Proportion harvest land cover (<15 yr)",
  "p_wetland" = "Proportion wetland land cover",
  "hu"        = "Human use intensity (IDW, 1 km resolution)",
  "tri"       = "Topographic Ruggedness Index (TRI)"
)

# Scale break labels for log-scaled x-axis
scale_breaks <- sort(unique(dat_raw$extent_radius_m))
scale_break_labels <- ifelse(
  scale_breaks < 1000,
  paste0(scale_breaks, " m"),
  paste0(round(scale_breaks / 1000, 1), " km")

# Build model formula lookup for figure subtitles.
# Each species x covariate maps to the model formula that produced its estimate.
build_formula_lookup <- function() {
  lookup <- tibble(species = character(), covariate = character(),
                   formula_label = character())

  # --- Helper to format covariate list ---
  fmt <- function(covs) paste(sort(covs), collapse = " + ")

  # === HORSE ===
  for (cv in horse_top5) {
    lookup <- bind_rows(lookup, tibble(
      species = "Horse", covariate = cv,
      formula_label = paste0("Base: ", fmt(horse_top5), " + SAC")
    ))
  }
  for (cv in horse_substituted) {
    sub_covs <- c(setdiff(horse_top5, horse_weakest), cv)
    lookup <- bind_rows(lookup, tibble(
      species = "Horse", covariate = cv,
      formula_label = paste0("Sub: ", fmt(sub_covs), " + SAC",
                             "  [", cv, " replaces ", horse_weakest, "]")
    ))
  }
  lookup <- bind_rows(lookup, tibble(
    species = "Horse", covariate = "NDVI_herb",
    formula_label = paste0("Sub: ", fmt(horse_ndvi_covars), " + SAC")
  ))

  # === CATTLE ===
  for (cv in cattle_top4) {
    lookup <- bind_rows(lookup, tibble(
      species = "Cattle", covariate = cv,
      formula_label = paste0("Base: ", fmt(cattle_top4), " + SAC")
    ))
  }
  for (cv in cattle_substituted) {
    sub_covs <- c(setdiff(cattle_top4, cattle_weakest), cv)
    lookup <- bind_rows(lookup, tibble(
      species = "Cattle", covariate = cv,
      formula_label = paste0("Sub: ", fmt(sub_covs), " + SAC",
                             "  [", cv, " replaces ", cattle_weakest, "]")
    ))
  }
  lookup <- bind_rows(lookup, tibble(
    species = "Cattle", covariate = "NDVI_herb",
    formula_label = paste0("Sub: ", fmt(cattle_ndvi_covars), " + SAC")
  ))

  # === ELK ===
  for (cv in elk_top2) {
    lookup <- bind_rows(lookup, tibble(
      species = "Elk", covariate = cv,
      formula_label = paste0("Base: ", fmt(elk_top2), " + SAC")
    ))
  }
  for (cv in elk_substituted) {
    sub_covs <- c(setdiff(elk_top2, elk_weakest), cv)
    lookup <- bind_rows(lookup, tibble(
      species = "Elk", covariate = cv,
      formula_label = paste0("Sub: ", fmt(sub_covs), " + SAC",
                             "  [", cv, " replaces ", elk_weakest, "]")
    ))
  }
  lookup <- bind_rows(lookup, tibble(
    species = "Elk", covariate = "NDVI_herb",
    formula_label = paste0("Sub: ", fmt(elk_ndvi_covars), " + SAC")
  ))

  return(lookup)
}

formula_lookup <- build_formula_lookup()

# Prepare plot data with factor levels and 95% CI bounds

plot_data_clean <- plot_data_clean %>%
  mutate(
    period = factor(period, levels = period_levels),
```

```{r scale-figures, fig.width=14, fig.height=12}
# Shared publication theme

# --- Helper: build a single species panel ---
# type = "multivariate" or "univariate"
build_species_panel <- function(mv_df, uni_df, species_name, covar_name,
                                y_lims, type, show_x_title = FALSE) {

  # Determine if this covariate is substituted for this species
  is_sub <- switch(species_name,
    "Horse"  = !(covar_name %in% horse_top5) &
               covar_name %in% c(horse_substituted, "NDVI_herb"),
    "Cattle" = !(covar_name %in% cattle_top4) &
               covar_name %in% c(cattle_substituted, "NDVI_herb"),
    "Elk"    = !(covar_name %in% elk_top2) &
               covar_name %in% c(elk_substituted, "NDVI_herb"),
    FALSE
  )

  base_title <- if (is_sub) paste0(species_name, " (sub)") else species_name

  get_subtitle <- function(sp) {
    lbl <- formula_lookup %>%
      filter(species == sp, covariate == covar_name) %>%
      pull(formula_label)
    if (length(lbl) == 0) return("")
    return(lbl)
  }

  if (type == "multivariate") {
    panel_title <- paste0(base_title, " \u2014 multivariate")
    panel_subtitle <- get_subtitle(species_name)
  } else {
    panel_title <- paste0(base_title, " \u2014 univariate")
    if (covar_name == "NDVI_herb") {
      panel_subtitle <- "Bivariate: NDVI_herb + p_herb + SAC"
    } else {
      panel_subtitle <- paste0(covar_name, " + SAC")
    }
  }

  x_lab <- if (show_x_title) "Spatial extent (buffer radius)" else NULL

  # === MULTIVARIATE PANEL ===
  if (type == "multivariate") {
    df <- mv_df

    if (species_name == "Horse") {
      # Monthly colored lines with ribbons
      p <- ggplot() +
        geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
        {if (nrow(df) > 0)
          geom_ribbon(data = df,
                      aes(x = extent_radius_m, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax,
                          fill = period, group = period), alpha = 0.12)
        } +
        {if (nrow(df) > 0)
          geom_line(data = df,
                    aes(x = extent_radius_m, y = estimate,
                        color = period, group = period), linewidth = 0.9)
        } +
        scale_color_manual(values = month_pal, name = "Month") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = month_pal, guide = "none")

    } else if (species_name == "Cattle") {
      # Bimonthly: black lines, solid vs dashed
      p <- ggplot() +
        geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
        {if (nrow(df) > 0)
          geom_ribbon(data = df,
                      aes(x = extent_radius_m, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax,
                          group = period), fill = "grey30", alpha = 0.1)
        } +
        {if (nrow(df) > 0)
          geom_line(data = df,
                    aes(x = extent_radius_m, y = estimate,
                        linetype = period, group = period),
                    color = "black", linewidth = 0.9)
        } +
        scale_linetype_manual(
          values = c("Jul-Aug" = "solid", "Sep-Oct" = "dashed"),
          name = "Bimonthly")

    } else {
      # Elk quarterly: grey lines, solid vs dashed
      p <- ggplot() +
        geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
        {if (nrow(df) > 0)
          geom_ribbon(data = df,
                      aes(x = extent_radius_m, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax,
                          group = period), fill = "grey30", alpha = 0.1)
        } +
        {if (nrow(df) > 0)
          geom_line(data = df,
                    aes(x = extent_radius_m, y = estimate,
                        linetype = period, group = period),
                    color = "grey30", linewidth = 1)
        } +
        scale_linetype_manual(
          values = c("May-Jul" = "solid", "Aug-Oct" = "dashed"),
          name = "Quarterly")
    }

  # === UNIVARIATE PANEL ===
  } else {
    df <- uni_df

    # All species: monthly colored lines with light ribbons
    p <- ggplot() +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
      {if (nrow(df) > 0)
        geom_ribbon(data = df,
                    aes(x = extent_radius_m, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax,
                        fill = period, group = period), alpha = 0.10)
      } +
      {if (nrow(df) > 0)
        geom_line(data = df,
                  aes(x = extent_radius_m, y = estimate,
                      color = period, group = period), linewidth = 0.7)
      } +
      scale_color_manual(values = month_pal, name = "Month") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = month_pal, guide = "none")
  }

  # Shared scales and labels
  p <- p +
    log_x_scale +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = y_lims) +
    labs(title = panel_title, subtitle = panel_subtitle,
         x = x_lab, y = "Std. coefficient") +
    pub_theme

  return(p)
}


# --- Main figure function: 3 rows x 2 columns per covariate ---
plot_covariate <- function(covar_name, plot_df) {

  # Subset data
  horse_mv  <- plot_df %>% filter(covariate == covar_name, species == "Horse",
                                   covar_source %in% c("base", "substituted"))
  horse_uni <- plot_df %>% filter(covariate == covar_name, species == "Horse",
                                   covar_source == "univariate")
  cattle_mv  <- plot_df %>% filter(covariate == covar_name, species == "Cattle",
                                    covar_source %in% c("base", "substituted"))
  cattle_uni <- plot_df %>% filter(covariate == covar_name, species == "Cattle",
                                    covar_source == "univariate")
  elk_mv  <- plot_df %>% filter(covariate == covar_name, species == "Elk",
                                 covar_source %in% c("base", "substituted"))
  elk_uni <- plot_df %>% filter(covariate == covar_name, species == "Elk",
                                 covar_source == "univariate")

  # Guard: return NULL if no data for this covariate
  all_est <- c(horse_mv$estimate, cattle_mv$estimate, elk_mv$estimate,
               horse_uni$estimate, cattle_uni$estimate, elk_uni$estimate)
  if (length(all_est) == 0 || all(is.na(all_est))) return(NULL)

  # Fixed y-axis limits for cross-covariate comparability
  y_lims <- c(-1, 1)

  # Build 6 panels (3 species x 2 types)
  p_h_mv  <- build_species_panel(horse_mv, horse_uni, "Horse", covar_name,
                                  y_lims, "multivariate")
  p_h_uni <- build_species_panel(horse_mv, horse_uni, "Horse", covar_name,
                                  y_lims, "univariate")
  p_c_mv  <- build_species_panel(cattle_mv, cattle_uni, "Cattle", covar_name,
                                  y_lims, "multivariate")
  p_c_uni <- build_species_panel(cattle_mv, cattle_uni, "Cattle", covar_name,
                                  y_lims, "univariate")
  p_e_mv  <- build_species_panel(elk_mv, elk_uni, "Elk", covar_name,
                                  y_lims, "multivariate", show_x_title = TRUE)
  p_e_uni <- build_species_panel(elk_mv, elk_uni, "Elk", covar_name,
                                  y_lims, "univariate", show_x_title = TRUE)

  # 3 rows x 2 columns, equal widths
  combined <- (p_h_mv | p_h_uni) /
              (p_c_mv | p_c_uni) /
              (p_e_mv | p_e_uni) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = covar_labels[covar_name],
      theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"))
    )

  return(combined)
}

# Generate all 7 figures
covar_plots <- map(habitat_covars, ~ plot_covariate(.x, plot_data_clean))
names(covar_plots) <- habitat_covars

for (cv in habitat_covars) {
  if (!is.null(covar_plots[[cv]])) {
    print(covar_plots[[cv]])
  }
}
```

# Summary Tables

## Covariate selection summary

```{r selection-summary}
# ── 1. Full covariate name lookup (Prop. shorthand) ──
# Named table_covar_labels to avoid overwriting covar_labels used by figures downstream
table_covar_labels <- c(
  tri       = "Terrain ruggedness index",
  hu        = "Human use",
  p_harvest = "Prop. harvest cutblock",
  p_wetland = "Prop. wetland",
  p_shrub   = "Prop. shrub",
  p_herb    = "Prop. herbaceous"
)

# ── 2. Assemble dredge-based rankings ──
selection_summary <- bind_rows(
  horse_selection$importance %>% mutate(species = "Horse"),
  cattle_selection$importance %>% mutate(species = "Cattle"),
  elk_selection$importance %>% mutate(species = "Elk")
) %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    budget = case_when(
      species == "Horse"  ~ covar_budget$Horse,
      species == "Cattle" ~ covar_budget$Cattle,
      species == "Elk"    ~ covar_budget$Elk
    ),
    is_sub = rank > budget,
    # Full covariate names; append "(sub.)" for substituted covariates
    covariate_full = paste0(table_covar_labels[covariate], if_else(is_sub, " (sub.)", ""))
  )

# ── 3. Determine substitution targets ──
# Non-base covariates replace the weakest base covariate
selection_summary <- selection_summary %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  mutate(
    weakest_base = table_covar_labels[covariate[rank == budget]],
    substituted_for = if_else(is_sub, weakest_base, "\u2014")
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# ── 4. Add NDVI_herb rows (excluded from dredge, evaluated via substitution) ──
ndvi_rows <- tibble(
  species = c("Horse", "Cattle", "Elk"),
  rank = NA_integer_,
  covariate = "NDVI_herb",
  cumulative_aic_weight = NA_real_,
  n_top_model = NA_integer_,
  n_models = NA_integer_,
  budget = c(covar_budget$Horse, covar_budget$Cattle, covar_budget$Elk),
  is_sub = TRUE,
  covariate_full = "Herbaceous NDVI (sub.)",
  weakest_base = NA_character_,
  substituted_for = c(
    # Horse: p_herb NOT in base -> drops weakest + second-weakest
    paste0(table_covar_labels[horse_weakest], " + ", table_covar_labels[horse_second_weakest], "\u2020"),
    # Cattle: p_herb IS in base -> drops weakest only
    paste0(table_covar_labels[cattle_weakest], "\u2021"),
    # Elk: budget = 2, p_herb not in base -> replaces entire base
    "Entire base model\u00a7"
  )
)

# ── 5. Assemble final table ──
selection_table <- bind_rows(selection_summary, ndvi_rows) %>%
  arrange(factor(species, levels = c("Horse", "Cattle", "Elk")), rank) %>%
  mutate(
    cumulative_aic_weight = round(cumulative_aic_weight, 1),
    rank = if_else(is.na(rank), "\u2014", as.character(rank))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Species = species,
    Rank = rank,
    Covariate = covariate_full,
    `Cumulative AIC weight` = cumulative_aic_weight,
    `N best model` = n_top_model,
    `Substituted for` = substituted_for
  )

# ── 6. Render table with flextable (Word-compatible output) ──
library(flextable)

# Caption and footnotes as separate strings for clean placement
table_caption <- paste0(
  "Table 1. Covariate selection outcomes based on cumulative variable importance (sum of Akaike weights across all models containing a given covariate, aggregated across spatial extents and temporal periods). Six covariates were screened at fixed model complexity equal to each species’ covariate budget; covariates ranked above the budget threshold formed the base model, while those marked (sub.) were evaluated via substitution. Herbaceous NDVI was excluded from the dredge (see Methods) and evaluated exclusively through substitution. "
)

ft <- flextable(selection_table) %>%
  # Column widths (inches) — total ~7" for US Letter with 1" margins
  width(j = "Species", width = 0.7) %>%
  width(j = "Rank", width = 0.5) %>%
  width(j = "Covariate", width = 1.8) %>%
  width(j = "Cumulative AIC weight", width = 1.1) %>%
  width(j = "N best model", width = 0.8) %>%
  width(j = "Substituted for", width = 2.1) %>%
  # Alignment
  align(j = c("Species", "Covariate", "Substituted for"), align = "left", part = "all") %>%
  align(j = "Rank", align = "center", part = "all") %>%
  align(j = c("Cumulative AIC weight", "N best model"), align = "right", part = "all") %>%
  # Font: Times New Roman 10pt (standard for ecology journals)
  font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") %>%
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") %>%
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "header") %>%
  bold(part = "header") %>%
  # Horizontal lines only (clean journal style)
  border_remove() %>%
  hline_top(border = fp_border(width = 1.5), part = "header") %>%
  hline_bottom(border = fp_border(width = 0.5), part = "header") %>%
  hline_bottom(border = fp_border(width = 1.5), part = "body") %>%
  # Species group dividers: light line between species blocks
  hline(i = which(selection_table$Species == "Horse" &
                    lead(selection_table$Species) == "Cattle"),
        border = fp_border(width = 0.5, style = "solid")) %>%
  hline(i = which(selection_table$Species == "Cattle" &
                    lead(selection_table$Species) == "Elk"),
        border = fp_border(width = 0.5, style = "solid")) %>%
  # Suppress repeated species names for cleaner look
  merge_v(j = "Species") %>%
  valign(j = "Species", valign = "top") %>%
  # Replace NA with em-dash
  colformat_double(na_str = "\u2014", digits = 1) %>%
  colformat_int(na_str = "\u2014") %>%
  # Caption
  set_caption(caption = table_caption) %>%
  # Footnotes
  add_footer_lines(values = c(
    paste0("\u2020 Prop. herbaceous was not in the horse base model; NDVI substitution replaced ",
           "the weakest (prop. shrub) and second-weakest (prop. wetland), substituting ",
           "herbaceous NDVI and forcing prop. herbaceous into the model."),
    paste0("\u2021 Prop. herbaceous was already in the cattle base model; NDVI substitution ",
           "replaced only the weakest base covariate (prop. wetland)."),
    paste0("\u00a7 With a covariate budget of 2, forcing both herbaceous NDVI and prop. ",
           "herbaceous replaced the entire elk base model; the NDVI estimate shares no ",
           "conditioning covariates with the base model.")
  )) %>%
  fontsize(size = 9, part = "footer") %>%
  font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "footer") %>%
  # Padding
  padding(padding.top = 2, padding.bottom = 2, part = "body")

ft

# ── 7. Export as standalone Word doc for easy copy-paste ──
# Disabled for JAE submission — docx convenience file and CSV not used by S1–S6 or Dryad.
# save_as_docx(ft, path = file.path(output_dir, "Table_1_covariate_selection.docx"))
# write_csv(selection_table, file.path(output_dir, "covariate_selection_summary.csv"))
```

## Domains of Scale

Each scale is classified into one of three domains based on its 95% CI:

- **Positive (+)**: lower CI > 0 (entire CI above zero)
- **Negative (−)**: upper CI < 0 (entire CI below zero)
- **Zero (0)**: CI spans zero

Contiguous runs of the same domain sign across the ordered scale continuum
form a single domain. Within each domain, the **scale of effect** is the
scale with the largest absolute standardized coefficient. All other scales
within the domain whose 95% CI overlaps that of the peak are reported as
**statistically indistinguishable peers** (i.e., we cannot confidently
distinguish the effect magnitude at those scales from the peak).

```{r domain-classification}
# ── 1. Classify each scale into a domain sign ──
# Work only with multivariate models (base + substituted)
mv_data <- plot_data_clean %>%
  filter(covar_source %in% c("base", "substituted")) %>%
  arrange(species, period, covariate, extent_radius_m)

domain_data <- mv_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Domain sign based on 95% CI position relative to zero
    domain_sign = case_when(
      conf.low > 0  ~ "+",
      conf.high < 0 ~ "-",
      TRUE           ~ "0"
    )
  )

# ── 2. Identify contiguous domains ──
# A new domain starts whenever the sign changes across adjacent scales
# within a species-period-covariate group
domain_data <- domain_data %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate) %>%
  mutate(
    sign_change = domain_sign != lag(domain_sign, default = first(domain_sign)),
    domain_id = cumsum(sign_change)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r domain-summary}
# ── 3. Summarise each domain ──
domain_summary <- domain_data %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate, domain_id, domain_sign) %>%
  summarise(
    n_scales       = n(),
    scale_min_m    = min(extent_radius_m),
    scale_max_m    = max(extent_radius_m),
    # Peak scale: highest absolute coefficient within domain
    peak_scale_m   = extent_radius_m[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    peak_estimate  = estimate[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    peak_se        = std.error[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    peak_ci_low    = conf.low[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    peak_ci_high   = conf.high[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    peak_p         = p.value[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(species, covariate, period, domain_id)

# ── Table render suppressed in SI ──
# The full domain-by-domain table runs to ~100 rows and is fully
# represented by (a) the manuscript domain table in §11.3 and (b) the
# multivariate domain bar chart (Key figures §1.2 / §11.4). The raw
# per-domain numbers are exported as domain_summary.csv.
cat(sprintf("Multivariate domain summary: %d rows (see domain_summary.csv for raw values).\n",
            nrow(domain_summary)))
```

```{r ci-overlap-peers}
# ── 4. Find scales with CIs overlapping the peak ──
# Two intervals [a1, b1] and [a2, b2] overlap iff a1 <= b2 AND a2 <= b1.
# For each domain, identify all scales whose CI overlaps the peak scale's CI.

# First, add peak CI bounds back to every row within its domain
domain_with_peak <- domain_data %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate, domain_id) %>%
  mutate(
    peak_idx       = which.max(abs(estimate)),
    peak_scale_m   = extent_radius_m[peak_idx],
    peak_ci_low    = conf.low[peak_idx],
    peak_ci_high   = conf.high[peak_idx],
    # Does this scale's CI overlap the peak's CI?
    overlaps_peak  = (conf.low <= peak_ci_high) & (peak_ci_low <= conf.high),
    is_peak        = (extent_radius_m == peak_scale_m)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Summarise peers per domain
peer_summary <- domain_with_peak %>%
  filter(overlaps_peak) %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate, domain_id) %>%
  summarise(
    domain_sign     = first(domain_sign),
    peak_scale_m    = first(peak_scale_m),
    peak_estimate   = estimate[is_peak][1],
    n_peers         = sum(!is_peak),
    peer_scales_m   = paste(extent_radius_m[!is_peak], collapse = ", "),
    all_scales_m    = paste(extent_radius_m, collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(species, covariate, period)

# ── Table render suppressed in SI ──
# The per-domain peer-scales table runs to ~80 rows. CI-overlap of peer
# scales with the peak scale is visualised as connecting brackets in the
# multivariate domain bar chart (Key figures §1.2 / §11.4). The raw list
# of peer scales per domain is exported as domain_peer_scales.csv.
cat(sprintf("Multivariate peer-scale summary: %d domains with one or more CI-overlapping peer scales.\n",
            nrow(peer_summary)))
```

## Manuscript table — Domain sign and peak scale of effect (not in manuscript)

Wide-format summary table: one row per period (species grouped by
`pack_rows`), one column per covariate. Cells show direction (+/−) and
peak scale. Blue = positive; red = negative; grey = no detectable
effect. Sign-flipping cells (Horse × human use, Sep and Oct) are
rendered as two stacked half-cells: blue on top with the fine-scale
positive peak, red on bottom with the broad-scale negative peak.
† = multiple non-zero domains; dominant shown.

```{r manuscript-table}
library(kableExtra)

# ── 1. Peak scale per non-zero domain ──
peak_per_domain <- domain_with_peak %>%
  filter(domain_sign != "0") %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate, domain_id) %>%
  summarise(
    domain_sign  = first(domain_sign),
    peak_scale_m = extent_radius_m[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    peak_est     = estimate[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    .groups      = "drop"
  )

# ── 2. Count domains per combination, flag sign-flipping ──
domain_counts <- peak_per_domain %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate) %>%
  summarise(
    n_nz_domains = n(),
    n_signs      = n_distinct(domain_sign),
    .groups      = "drop"
  )

# ── 3. Helpers ──
fmt_scale <- function(m) {
  ifelse(m >= 1000, paste0(round(m / 1000, 1), " km"), paste0(m, " m"))
}

# Single-value cell: flexbox centres content and fills the full TD height.
# height:100% works here because every TD has an explicit height set via
# extra_css in the column_spec loop (step 11).
make_div <- function(text, bg, fg, bold = TRUE, font_size = "12px") {
  bld <- if (bold) "font-weight:bold;" else ""
  paste0(
    '<div style="height:100%;display:flex;align-items:center;',
    'justify-content:center;background:', bg, ';color:', fg, ';',
    bld, 'font-size:', font_size, ';padding:3px 5px;box-sizing:border-box;">',
    text, '</div>'
  )
}

# Flip cell: outer div fills full TD height as a flex column;
# each half gets flex:1 so they share the height equally.
# Slightly smaller font (10px) so two lines fit cleanly.
make_flip_div <- function(pos_text, neg_text) {
  half <- paste0(
    'display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;',
    'flex:1;color:white;font-weight:bold;font-size:10px;padding:2px 4px;'
  )
  paste0(
    '<div style="height:100%;display:flex;flex-direction:column;">',
    '<div style="background:#0072B2;', half, '">', pos_text, '</div>',
    '<div style="background:#B22222;', half, '">', neg_text, '</div>',
    '</div>'
  )
}

# ── 4a. Regular cells (no sign-flipping) ──
dominant_regular <- peak_per_domain %>%
  left_join(domain_counts, by = c("species", "period", "covariate")) %>%
  filter(n_signs == 1) %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate) %>%
  slice_max(abs(peak_est), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    sign_char = ifelse(domain_sign == "+", "+", "\u2212"),
    raw_text  = paste0(sign_char, fmt_scale(peak_scale_m)),
    raw_text  = ifelse(n_nz_domains > 1, paste0(raw_text, "\u2020"), raw_text),
    bg        = ifelse(domain_sign == "+", "#0072B2", "#B22222"),
    cell      = make_div(raw_text, bg = bg, fg = "white"),
    cell_sign = domain_sign
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, covariate, cell, cell_sign)

# ── 4b. Sign-flipping cells — flex-column container, two equal halves ──
flip_cells <- peak_per_domain %>%
  left_join(domain_counts, by = c("species", "period", "covariate")) %>%
  filter(n_signs > 1) %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate) %>%
  summarise(
    pos_peak_m = peak_scale_m[domain_sign == "+"],
    neg_peak_m = peak_scale_m[domain_sign == "-"],
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    cell = make_flip_div(
      pos_text = paste0("+", fmt_scale(pos_peak_m), "\u2020"),
      neg_text = paste0("\u2212", fmt_scale(neg_peak_m))
    ),
    cell_sign = "flip"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, covariate, cell, cell_sign)

# ── 5. Combine ──
all_cells <- bind_rows(dominant_regular, flip_cells)

# ── 6. Covariate display labels ──
covar_abbrev <- c(
  "p_herb"    = "Herb. cover",
  "NDVI_herb" = "Herb. NDVI",
  "p_shrub"   = "Shrub",
  "p_harvest" = "Harvest",
  "p_wetland" = "Wetland",
  "hu"        = "Human use",
  "tri"       = "TRI"
)
col_labels <- unname(covar_abbrev)

# ── 7. Period ordering ──
period_order <- c(
  "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct",
  "Jul-Aug", "Sep-Oct",
  "May-Jul",  "Aug-Oct"
)

# ── 8. Pivot to wide ──
table_long <- all_cells %>%
  mutate(
    species     = factor(species, levels = c("Horse", "Cattle", "Elk")),
    period      = factor(period,  levels = period_order),
    covar_short = covar_abbrev[as.character(covariate)]
  ) %>%
  arrange(species, period)

cell_wide <- table_long %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, covar_short, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from  = covar_short, values_from = cell,
              # Zero-only cells: grey flexbox div, same height/structure as others
              values_fill = make_div("\u2014", bg = "#F0F0F0",
                                     fg = "#999999", bold = FALSE)) %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, all_of(col_labels))

# ── 9. Display table — Period only (species via pack_rows) ──
# Horse periods spelled out in full; cattle/elk range periods kept short.
period_display <- c(
  "May" = "May",       "Jun" = "June",      "Jul" = "July",
  "Aug" = "August",    "Sep" = "September", "Oct" = "October",
  "Jul-Aug" = "Jul\u2013Aug", "Sep-Oct" = "Sep\u2013Oct",
  "May-Jul" = "May\u2013Jul", "Aug-Oct" = "Aug\u2013Oct"
)
table_display <- cell_wide %>%
  dplyr::select(Period = period, all_of(col_labels)) %>%
  mutate(Period = period_display[as.character(Period)])

# Plain CSV with HTML stripped
# Disabled for JAE submission — manuscript-table CSV not used by S1–S6 or Dryad.
# write_csv(
#   table_display %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~ gsub("<[^>]+>", "", .x))),
#   file.path(output_dir, "scale_of_effect_manuscript_table.csv")
# )

# ── 10. Build kable ──
tbl <- kbl(
  table_display,
  format  = "html",
  escape  = FALSE,
  caption = paste0(
    "Domain sign and peak scale of effect for each species \u00d7 period ",
    "\u00d7 covariate combination. Peak scale = buffer radius with largest ",
    "|\u03B2| within the dominant non-zero domain. ",
    "Blue = positive; red = negative; grey = no detectable effect ",
    "(95% CI spans zero at all scales). ",
    "Vertically split cells (Horse \u00d7 human use, September and October): ",
    "blue (upper) = fine-scale positive peak; red (lower) = broad-scale negative peak. ",
    "\u2020 = multiple non-zero domains; dominant shown."
  ),
  align = rep("c", length(col_labels) + 1)  # all columns centre-justified
) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("condensed"),
    full_width        = FALSE,
    font_size         = 13
  ) %>%
  pack_rows("Horse",  1, 6, bold = TRUE, hline_after = TRUE) %>%
  pack_rows("Cattle", 7, 8, bold = TRUE, hline_after = TRUE) %>%
  pack_rows("Elk",    9, 10, bold = TRUE)

# ── 11. Fix TD dimensions and add hard black borders ──
# height:44px gives every TD an explicit height so that child divs can
# use height:100% to fill it completely — this eliminates the white gap
# around stacked flip-cell divs.
# width:78px makes all data columns the same width.
# padding:0 removes default cell padding so divs fill edge-to-edge.
DATA_CSS <- paste0(
  "padding:0 !important;",
  "height:44px !important;",
  "width:78px !important;",
  "min-width:78px !important;",
  "border:1px solid #333 !important;",
  "vertical-align:middle !important;"
)
for (j in seq_along(col_labels)) {
  tbl <- tbl %>%
    column_spec(j + 1, extra_css = DATA_CSS)   # +1 for Period column
}
# Period column: border only (no fixed width needed)
tbl <- tbl %>%
  column_spec(1, extra_css = "border:1px solid #333 !important;")

tbl

# ── 12. Word export via flextable ──
# kableExtra HTML cannot export to .docx; rebuild from plain text data.
# Flip cells: two-line text (+peak\n−peak) with purple background —
# Word does not support split cells, so purple signals sign-flipping.

plain_regular <- peak_per_domain %>%
  left_join(domain_counts, by = c("species", "period", "covariate")) %>%
  filter(n_signs == 1) %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate) %>%
  slice_max(abs(peak_est), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    sign_char = ifelse(domain_sign == "+", "+", "\u2212"),
    cell_text = paste0(sign_char, fmt_scale(peak_scale_m)),
    cell_text = ifelse(n_nz_domains > 1, paste0(cell_text, "\u2020"), cell_text),
    cell_sign = domain_sign
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, covariate, cell_text, cell_sign)

plain_flip <- peak_per_domain %>%
  left_join(domain_counts, by = c("species", "period", "covariate")) %>%
  filter(n_signs > 1) %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate) %>%
  summarise(
    pos_text = paste0("+",       fmt_scale(peak_scale_m[domain_sign == "+"]), "\u2020"),
    neg_text = paste0("\u2212",  fmt_scale(peak_scale_m[domain_sign == "-"])),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    cell_text = paste0(pos_text, "\n", neg_text),
    cell_sign = "flip"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, covariate, cell_text, cell_sign)

all_plain <- bind_rows(plain_regular, plain_flip)

plain_long <- all_plain %>%
  mutate(
    species     = factor(species, levels = c("Horse", "Cattle", "Elk")),
    period      = factor(period,  levels = period_order),
    covar_short = covar_abbrev[as.character(covariate)]
  ) %>%
  arrange(species, period)

plain_cell_wide <- plain_long %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, covar_short, cell_text) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from  = covar_short, values_from = cell_text,
              values_fill = "\u2014") %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, all_of(col_labels))

plain_sign_wide <- plain_long %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, covar_short, cell_sign) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from  = covar_short, values_from = cell_sign,
              values_fill = "0") %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, all_of(col_labels))

word_display <- plain_cell_wide %>%
  mutate(
    Species = as.character(species),
    Period  = period_display[as.character(period)]
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Species, Period, all_of(col_labels))

ft2 <- flextable(word_display) %>%
  width(j = "Species",   width = 0.65) %>%
  width(j = "Period",    width = 0.90) %>%
  width(j = col_labels,  width = 0.78) %>%   # 7 × 0.78" ≈ 5.46"; total ~7.0"
  font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") %>%
  fontsize(size = 9,  part = "body") %>%
  fontsize(size = 9,  part = "header") %>%
  bold(part = "header") %>%
  align(j = "Species", align = "left",   part = "all") %>%
  align(j = "Period",  align = "center", part = "all") %>%
  align(j = col_labels, align = "center", part = "all") %>%
  valign(valign = "center", part = "body") %>%
  merge_v(j = "Species") %>%
  valign(j = "Species", valign = "top", part = "body") %>%
  border_remove() %>%
  hline_top(border    = fp_border(width = 1.5), part = "header") %>%
  hline_bottom(border = fp_border(width = 0.75), part = "header") %>%
  hline_bottom(border = fp_border(width = 1.5), part = "body") %>%
  hline(i = 6, border = fp_border(width = 0.5, style = "solid"), part = "body") %>%
  hline(i = 8, border = fp_border(width = 0.5, style = "solid"), part = "body") %>%
  set_caption(caption = paste0(
    "Table 2. Domain sign and peak scale of effect for each species \u00d7 period ",
    "\u00d7 covariate combination. Peak scale = buffer radius with largest |\u03B2| ",
    "within the dominant non-zero domain. ",
    "Blue = positive effect; red = negative effect; grey = no detectable effect; ",
    "purple = sign-flipping (positive at fine, negative at broad scales or vice versa). ",
    "\u2020 Multiple non-zero domains present; dominant shown."
  )) %>%
  add_footer_lines(
    values = "\u2020 Multiple non-zero domains present; dominant (largest |\u03B2|) shown."
  ) %>%
  fontsize(size = 8, part = "footer") %>%
  font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "footer") %>%
  padding(padding.top = 3, padding.bottom = 3, part = "body")

# Apply per-cell background and font colour
n_word_rows <- nrow(word_display)
for (j in seq_along(col_labels)) {
  col_name <- col_labels[j]
  signs <- if (col_name %in% names(plain_sign_wide)) plain_sign_wide[[col_name]] else rep("0", n_word_rows)
  signs[is.na(signs)] <- "0"
  for (i in seq_len(n_word_rows)) {
    bg_col <- switch(signs[i],
      "+"    = "#0072B2",

      "flip" = "#7B5EA7",
               "#F0F0F0"
    )
    fg_col <- if (signs[i] == "0") "#888888" else "white"
    ft2 <- ft2 %>%
      bg(i = i,    j = col_name, bg    = bg_col, part = "body") %>%
      color(i = i, j = col_name, color = fg_col, part = "body")
  }
}
```

## Scale-of-effect variability across the growing season (horse) (Table 2 in manuscript)

We summarise how consistent the peak scale of effect is across horse
monthly profiles (May–October, n = 6). For each covariate the peak is
the *global peak* of the monthly profile — the scale with the largest |β̂|
across all non-zero domains (same dominant-domain rule as the
table in §11.3). We report (i) the number of months with a
detected non-zero dominant domain, (ii) the range of peak buffer class
across detections, and (iii) the SD of peak buffer class when three or
more months contributed. Buffer class indexes the log-spaced scale grid
(1 = 40 m; 16 = 7223 m; adjacent classes differ by a factor of ~√2 in
radius). Cattle and elk are excluded from this table because
their temporal grain (bimonthly and quarterly, respectively) yields at
most n = 2 periods per covariate, which is insufficient for either a
range or an SD-based variability estimate to be meaningful.

```{r scale-of-effect-variability}
# ── Temporal variability of peak buffer class (horse) ──
# Derives, per covariate for horse only:
#   - number of months (out of 6) with a non-zero dominant (global)
#     domain detected
#   - range of peak buffer class across detected months, on the
#     log-spaced grid indexed 1 (40 m) to 16 (7223 m)
#   - SD of peak buffer class, only when n_detected >= 3 (n=2 reduces
#     to a single pairwise difference, n<=1 has no spread)
# Inputs (already in memory from §11.2):
#   - domain_summary: one row per (species, period, covariate, domain)
#   - scale_breaks:   ordered buffer radii in metres (length 16)

# Global peak per (period, covariate) for horse: the non-zero domain
# with the largest |peak_estimate|. Mirrors the dominant-domain rule
# used for the §11.3 manuscript table. Buffer-class index is matched
# against scale_breaks so that the table uses ordinal units (1–16)
# rather than raw metres.
profile_global_peak_horse <- domain_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(species == "Horse",
                domain_sign %in% c("+", "-")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(period, covariate) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(abs(peak_estimate), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(peak_class = match(peak_scale_m, scale_breaks))

# Display metadata: spelled-out covariate labels and type grouping.
# Type distinguishes layers that are recomputed per period (temporal)
# from layers computed once across the study period (static).
covar_meta <- tibble::tribble(
  ~covariate,     ~cov_label,                   ~cov_type,
  "NDVI_herb",    "Herbaceous NDVI",            "Temporal",
  "hu",           "Human use intensity",        "Temporal",
  "p_harvest",    "Prop. harvest",              "Static",
  "p_herb",       "Prop. herbaceous",           "Static",
  "p_shrub",      "Prop. shrub",                "Static",
  "p_wetland",    "Prop. wetland",              "Static",
  "tri",          "Terrain ruggedness index",   "Static"
)

# Horse has 6 possible monthly periods (May–October). The denominator
# is fixed at 6 rather than derived from the data to keep the metric
# well-defined even if a covariate has zero detections across all
# months (in which case it still shows as "0/6").
n_horse_periods <- 6L

# Build the covariate grid so that any covariate with zero detections
# still appears as a row (rendered as "—"). Covariate ordering is
# inherited from covar_meta.
soE_variability_horse <- tibble::tibble(covariate = covar_meta$covariate) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    profile_global_peak_horse %>%
      dplyr::group_by(covariate) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(
        n_detected = dplyr::n(),
        peak_min   = min(peak_class),
        peak_max   = max(peak_class),
        # SD only reported at n >= 3 (see intro prose for rationale)
        peak_sd    = if (dplyr::n() >= 3) round(stats::sd(peak_class), 2)
                     else NA_real_,
        .groups    = "drop"
      ),
    by = "covariate"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(n_detected = dplyr::coalesce(n_detected, 0L)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(covar_meta, by = "covariate") %>%
  # Build the compact "Range [SD]" cell. case_when branches are mutually
  # exclusive by n_detected and then by whether the two peaks at n=2 are
  # equal (degenerate range).
  dplyr::mutate(
    det_rate = sprintf("%d/%d", n_detected, n_horse_periods),
    range_sd = dplyr::case_when(
      n_detected == 0             ~ "\u2014",
      n_detected == 1             ~ as.character(peak_min),
      n_detected >= 3             ~ sprintf("%d\u2013%d [%.2f]",
                                            peak_min, peak_max, peak_sd),
      peak_min == peak_max        ~ paste0(peak_min, "*"),
      TRUE                        ~ sprintf("%d\u2013%d*",
                                            peak_min, peak_max)
    ),
    cov_label = factor(cov_label, levels = covar_meta$cov_label)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(cov_label) %>%
  dplyr::select(Covariate             = cov_label,
                Type             = cov_type,
                `Months with domain`  = det_rate,
                `Range [SD]`          = range_sd)

# ── Render table with flextable (Word-compatible output) ──
# Style matches Tables 1 and 2: Times New Roman 10pt, bold header, thick
# outer rules + thin header rule, light divider between temporal and
# static blocks, em-dash for NA. Caption built as a separate string for
# clean placement.
table_3_caption <- paste(
  "Table 3. Scale-of-effect variability across horse monthly profiles",
  "(May\u2013October, n = 6). Peak buffer class is the log-spaced grid",
  "index (1 = 40 m, 16 = 7223 m; adjacent classes differ by a factor",
  "of ~\u221A2 in radius). 'Months with domain' is the number of months",
  "(of 6) in which a non-zero dominant domain was detected. Range is",
  "the minimum\u2013maximum peak buffer class across detected months.",
  "SD is reported in brackets only when three or more months",
  "contributed; at n = 2, SD reduces to a single pairwise difference",
  "and is not a variability estimate (flagged with *). Covariate type",
  "distinguishes temporally varying layers (recalculated monthly) from",
  "static layers (computed once across the study period). Cattle and",
  "elk are excluded because their temporal grain yields at most n = 2",
  "periods per covariate."
)

ft3 <- flextable(soE_variability_horse) %>%
  # Column widths (inches) — total ~6" fits comfortably on US Letter
  width(j = "Covariate",          width = 2.0) %>%
  width(j = "Type",               width = 1.0) %>%
  width(j = "Months with domain", width = 1.4) %>%
  width(j = "Range [SD]",         width = 1.6) %>%
  # Alignment: text left, numeric-ish centred
  align(j = c("Covariate", "Type"),  align = "left",   part = "all") %>%
  align(j = "Months with domain",    align = "center", part = "all") %>%
  align(j = "Range [SD]",            align = "center", part = "all") %>%
  # Font: Times New Roman 10pt (standard for ecology journals)
  font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") %>%
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") %>%
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "header") %>%
  bold(part = "header") %>%
  # Horizontal rules only (clean journal style)
  border_remove() %>%
  hline_top(border    = fp_border(width = 1.5), part = "header") %>%
  hline_bottom(border = fp_border(width = 0.5), part = "header") %>%
  hline_bottom(border = fp_border(width = 1.5), part = "body")  %>%
  # Light divider between the two temporal rows and the five static rows.
  # Covariate order is fixed by covar_meta: rows 1–2 are temporal
  # (NDVI_herb, hu); rows 3–7 are static.
  hline(i = 2, border = fp_border(width = 0.5, style = "solid"),
        part = "body") %>%
  # Caption
  set_caption(caption = table_3_caption) %>%
  # Footnotes. Use Unicode en-dash/em-dash consistent with body.
  add_footer_lines(values = c(
    paste0("* Range shown only; SD not reported because n = 2 detected ",
           "months reduces to a single pairwise difference and is not a ",
           "variability estimate."),
    paste0("\u2014 Covariate had no detected non-zero dominant domain in ",
           "any month (n = 0).")
  )) %>%
  fontsize(size = 9, part = "footer") %>%
  font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "footer") %>%
  padding(padding.top = 2, padding.bottom = 2, part = "body")

ft3
```
