## Domain Visualization (Figure 2 in manuscript)

Horizontal bars spanning the scale continuum, coloured by domain sign.
Diamonds mark the peak scale of effect within each non-zero domain;
coloured stars (★) mark the global peak; colour matches domain sign (blue/red).
Species are grouped with visual separation; periods are ordered
chronologically (earliest at top). Animal silhouette icons identify
species groups.

```{r domain-bars, fig.width=14, fig.height=16, cache=FALSE}
# ============================================================================
# Domain bar chart — refactored from facet_wrap to individual patchwork panels
# to support: (1) custom legend in 8th position, (2) animal icons per panel,
# (3) brackets connecting same-sign split-domain peaks, (4) global-peak star markers.
# ============================================================================

# ── Palettes ──
# Okabe-Ito colorblind-safe palette: blue (positive), vermillion (negative), grey (zero)
# Greyscale-distinguishable shades of the canonical Okabe-Ito blue and firebrick:
# darken the red aggressively (amount = 0.50) so its lightness drops well below the
# blue's. Lightness (the L in HCL), not alpha or chroma, is what controls grayscale
# separation — alpha just blends toward the background and preserves the L ratio,
# chroma changes vividness without moving L. Hue is preserved, so the palette
# stays colourblind-safe under the common colour vision deficiencies.
neg_col <- colorspace::darken("#B22222", amount = 0.50)  # very dark firebrick (greyscale-safe)
pos_col <- "#0072B2"                                     # Okabe-Ito blue (unchanged)
domain_pal <- c("-" = neg_col, "0" = "grey85", "+" = pos_col)

# ── Y-axis ordering ──
# Species order top→bottom: Horse, Cattle, Elk.
# ggplot places the LAST factor level at the top of a discrete y-axis, so
# the species order is reversed (Elk first, Horse last) and within each
# species block periods are listed latest-first (earliest period at top).
species_period_order <- c(
  # Elk (quarterly) — rows 1–2; earliest at top of Elk block
  "Elk - Aug-Oct", "Elk - May-Jul",
  # Cattle (bimonthly) — rows 3–4; earliest at top of Cattle block
  "Cattle - Sep-Oct", "Cattle - Jul-Aug",
  # Horse (monthly) — rows 5–10; May at top (pos 10), Oct at bottom of Horse block
  "Horse - Oct", "Horse - Sep", "Horse - Aug",
  "Horse - Jul", "Horse - Jun", "Horse - May"
)

# Period-only labels for annotation between icons and bars.
# Positioned at x = 28 m (geometric midpoint of icon_xmax and first scale break).
# These appear in every panel; species names are added separately (left column only).
period_label_data <- tibble(
  row_label   = factor(species_period_order, levels = species_period_order),
  # Order matches species_period_order: Elk (2) → Cattle (2) → Horse (6)
  # Range periods kept abbreviated; horse single months spelled out.
  period_text = c("Aug–Oct", "May–Jul",
                  "Sep–Oct", "Jul–Aug",
                  "October", "September", "August", "July", "June", "May")
)

# ── Main bar data (one row per domain) ──
bar_data <- domain_summary %>%
  mutate(
    covar_label = covar_labels[as.character(covariate)],
    row_label   = paste(species, "-", as.character(period)),
    row_label   = factor(row_label, levels = species_period_order)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(row_label))

# ── Peak classification: regular peaks vs global peak ──
# When multiple non-zero domains exist for the same species × period × covariate,
# the domain with the largest |peak estimate| is flagged as the "global peak"
# and plotted as a coloured star (★) matching the domain sign palette.
peak_data <- bar_data %>%
  filter(domain_sign != "0") %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate, covar_label) %>%
  mutate(
    n_nz_domains   = n(),
    # Global peak = largest |estimate| across all non-zero domains.
    # For single-domain profiles this is always the one peak;
    # for multi-domain profiles it distinguishes the dominant peak from secondary ones.
    is_global_peak = abs(peak_estimate) == max(abs(peak_estimate))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

regular_peaks <- peak_data %>% filter(!is_global_peak)
global_peaks  <- peak_data %>% filter(is_global_peak)

# ── Bracket data: connect peaks of same-sign split domains with overlapping CIs ──
# When a species × period × covariate has multiple non-zero domains of the SAME
# sign separated by a zero domain, and the peak CIs of those domains overlap,
# draw a bracket connecting the two peak positions. This communicates that the
# separated domains are statistically indistinguishable in effect magnitude.
# All 21/22 such pairs qualify; the sole exception is Elk | May-Jul | p_herb.
bracket_data <- peak_data %>%
  filter(domain_sign != "0") %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate, covar_label, domain_sign) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%                        # must have 2+ same-sign domains
  arrange(peak_scale_m, .by_group = TRUE) %>%  # order by position for pairing
  reframe({
    # For each pair of same-sign domains, check CI overlap
    pairs <- combn(seq_len(n()), 2, simplify = FALSE)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs, function(idx) {
      i <- idx[1]; j <- idx[2]
      ci_overlap <- peak_ci_low[i] <= peak_ci_high[j] &
                    peak_ci_low[j] <= peak_ci_high[i]
      if (ci_overlap) {
        tibble(
          row_label = row_label[i],        # same for both (same spp × period)
          x_start   = peak_scale_m[i],     # left peak
          x_end     = peak_scale_m[j],     # right peak
          bracket_sign = domain_sign[i]
        )
      } else {
        tibble()
      }
    }))
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Compute y offset: shift bracket above the bar
  # row_label is a factor — numeric position + offset for bracket height.
  # Bracket colour matches the domain sign for visual distinction from grey dividers.
  mutate(
    y_num  = as.numeric(row_label),
    y_base = y_num + 0.35,
    bracket_col = ifelse(bracket_sign == "+", pos_col, neg_col)
  )

# ── Load animal silhouette icons ──
# Helper: convert any PNG array to RGBA and set semi-transparent silhouettes.
# Handles grayscale (1-ch), grayscale+alpha (2-ch), RGB (3-ch), RGBA (4-ch).
ensure_transparent <- function(img, alpha_value = 0.60) {
  nr <- dim(img)[1]; nc <- dim(img)[2]
  nch <- if (is.null(dim(img)[3])) 1L else dim(img)[3]

  # Normalise to 4-channel RGBA
  rgba <- array(0, dim = c(nr, nc, 4))
  if (nch == 1) {
    # Grayscale only — no alpha
    rgba[,,1] <- rgba[,,2] <- rgba[,,3] <- img
    rgba[,,4] <- 1
  } else if (nch == 2) {
    # Grayscale + alpha (mode LA) — the case for these silhouette PNGs
    rgba[,,1] <- rgba[,,2] <- rgba[,,3] <- img[,,1]
    rgba[,,4] <- img[,,2]
  } else if (nch == 3) {
    # RGB — no alpha
    rgba[,,1:3] <- img
    rgba[,,4]   <- 1
  } else {
    # RGBA
    rgba <- img
  }

  # Make white/near-white pixels fully transparent; darken the rest to alpha_value
  white_mask <- rgba[,,1] > 0.9 & rgba[,,2] > 0.9 & rgba[,,3] > 0.9
  rgba[,,4][white_mask]  <- 0
  rgba[,,4][!white_mask] <- pmin(rgba[,,4][!white_mask], alpha_value)
  rgba
}

# Tint silhouette pixels to a flat RGB colour (0–1 scale per channel).
# Preserves the alpha mask from ensure_transparent; replaces grayscale with target hue.
colorize_icon <- function(rgba, r, g, b) {
  mask <- rgba[,,4] > 0.05   # non-transparent (silhouette) pixels
  rgba[,,1][mask] <- r
  rgba[,,2][mask] <- g
  rgba[,,3][mask] <- b
  rgba
}

# Load icons and apply species-specific colours
#   Horse: warm brown  (#8B4513 saddlebrown)
#   Cow:   near-black  (#111111)
#   Elk:   dark grey   (#555555)
horse_img <- colorize_icon(
  ensure_transparent(readPNG(file.path(base_path, "input", "horse.png"))),
  r = 0.361, g = 0.180, b = 0.039   # #5C2E0A — dark chestnut brown
)
cow_img <- colorize_icon(
  ensure_transparent(readPNG(file.path(base_path, "input", "cow.png")), alpha_value = 0.95),
  r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0   # pure black — alpha raised to 0.95 so it composites black, not dark grey
)
elk_img <- colorize_icon(
  ensure_transparent(readPNG(file.path(base_path, "input", "elk.png"))),
  r = 0.439, g = 0.502, b = 0.565   # #708090 — slate blue-grey
)

# Icon placement: x in metres (left of data range on log axis), y = species centres.
# Numeric y values map to discrete factor positions (1 = first level at bottom).
# Elk rows: 1–2 (centre 1.5), Cattle: 3–4 (centre 3.5), Horse: 5–10 (centre 7.5)
icon_xmin <- 5.5  # metres — shifted further left to free space for period labels
icon_xmax <- 11   # metres — narrowed to match leftward shift

# ── Species separator positions ──
sep_positions <- c(
  2.5,  # between Elk (positions 1–2) and Cattle (positions 3–4)
  4.5   # between Cattle (positions 3–4) and Horse (positions 5–10)
)

# ── Shared axis limits (log10-scale x, consistent across all panels) ──
# Left limit extended to 4 m (from 7 m) so that species-name annotations at x = 5.5 m
# fall within the coordinate system and are not dropped. No scale breaks exist below 40 m,
# so the extra space (4–7 m) is invisible white space that merges with the icon zone.
x_lims <- c(3.5, max(scale_breaks) * 1.15)

# ── Panel builder ──
build_domain_panel <- function(cv_label,
                               show_x_title  = FALSE,
                               show_y_labels = TRUE) {
  # Subset data for this covariate
  d      <- bar_data      %>% filter(covar_label == cv_label)
  rp     <- regular_peaks %>% filter(covar_label == cv_label)
  gp     <- global_peaks  %>% filter(covar_label == cv_label)
  br     <- bracket_data  %>% filter(covar_label == cv_label)
  br_pos <- br %>% filter(bracket_sign == "+")
  br_neg <- br %>% filter(bracket_sign == "-")

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(y = row_label)) +
    # ── Species separator lines ──
    geom_hline(yintercept = sep_positions, linetype = "solid",
               colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
    # ── Domain-span bars (standard hue) ──
    geom_segment(aes(x = scale_min_m, xend = scale_max_m,
                     yend = row_label, colour = domain_sign),
                 linewidth = 4, lineend = "round") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = domain_pal, guide = "none") +
    # ── Regular peak markers (filled diamond with black outline — fill matches domain sign) ──
    # shape 23 = filled diamond; fill = domain colour, colour = black border.
    # scale_fill_manual below maps domain_sign to domain_pal for both this layer
    # and any other fill-mapped layers.
    geom_point(data = rp, aes(x = peak_scale_m, fill = domain_sign),
               shape = 23, size = 3.2, colour = "black", stroke = 0.9) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = domain_pal, guide = "none") +
    # ── Global peak markers (ggstar filled star) ──
    # geom_star() provides fill + colour (border) aesthetics like shape 23.
    # fill maps to domain_sign via the existing scale_fill_manual(domain_pal).
    # starshape = 1 is a regular 5-pointed star.
    geom_star(data = gp, aes(x = peak_scale_m, y = row_label, fill = domain_sign),
              starshape = 1, colour = "black", starstroke = 0.9, size = 4.0,
              inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    # ── Brackets connecting same-sign split-domain peaks with overlapping CIs ──
    # Horizontal bracket above the bar connects peak positions across a zero gap,
    # indicating the two domains are statistically indistinguishable.
    # ── Positive-sign brackets (blue) ──
    {if (nrow(br_pos) > 0)
      list(
        geom_segment(data = br_pos, aes(x = x_start, xend = x_end,
                     y = y_base, yend = y_base),
                     linewidth = 0.9, colour = pos_col,
                     lineend = "butt", inherit.aes = FALSE),
        geom_segment(data = br_pos, aes(x = x_start, xend = x_start,
                     y = y_num + 0.18, yend = y_base),
                     linewidth = 0.9, colour = pos_col,
                     inherit.aes = FALSE),
        geom_segment(data = br_pos, aes(x = x_end, xend = x_end,
                     y = y_num + 0.18, yend = y_base),
                     linewidth = 0.9, colour = pos_col,
                     inherit.aes = FALSE)
      )
    else NULL} +
    # ── Negative-sign brackets (red) ──
    {if (nrow(br_neg) > 0)
      list(
        geom_segment(data = br_neg, aes(x = x_start, xend = x_end,
                     y = y_base, yend = y_base),
                     linewidth = 0.9, colour = neg_col,
                     lineend = "butt", inherit.aes = FALSE),
        geom_segment(data = br_neg, aes(x = x_start, xend = x_start,
                     y = y_num + 0.18, yend = y_base),
                     linewidth = 0.9, colour = neg_col,
                     inherit.aes = FALSE),
        geom_segment(data = br_neg, aes(x = x_end, xend = x_end,
                     y = y_num + 0.18, yend = y_base),
                     linewidth = 0.9, colour = neg_col,
                     inherit.aes = FALSE)
      )
    else NULL} +
    # ── Period labels (between icon and bars, all panels) ──
    # Anchored at x = 30 m with hjust = 1 (right-justified); right edge at 30 m
    # leaves ~10 m of clear space before the first 40 m bar on the log scale.
    geom_text(data = period_label_data,
              aes(x = 30, y = row_label, label = period_text),
              hjust = 1, size = 3.0, colour = "black",
              inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    # ── Animal silhouette icons ──
    # Icons centred on each species band. Elk occupies rows 1–2 (band 0.5–2.5),
    # Cattle rows 3–4 (2.5–4.5), Horse rows 5–10 (4.5–10.5). Icon heights are
    # preserved from the previous horse-at-bottom layout (2.0, 1.4, 1.8 units).
    annotation_custom(
      grob = rasterGrob(elk_img, interpolate = TRUE),
      xmin = icon_xmin, xmax = icon_xmax, ymin = 0.6, ymax = 2.4
    ) +
    annotation_custom(
      grob = rasterGrob(cow_img, interpolate = TRUE),
      xmin = icon_xmin, xmax = icon_xmax, ymin = 2.8, ymax = 4.2
    ) +
    annotation_custom(
      grob = rasterGrob(horse_img, interpolate = TRUE),
      xmin = icon_xmin, xmax = icon_xmax, ymin = 6.5, ymax = 8.5
    ) +
    # ── Axes and scales ──
    scale_x_log10(
      breaks = scale_breaks,
      labels = scale_break_labels,
      limits = x_lims
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(
      title = cv_label,
      x     = if (show_x_title) "Spatial extent (buffer radius)" else NULL,
      y     = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
      axis.text.y        = element_blank(),  # replaced by annotate below (species) + geom_text (periods)
      axis.title         = element_text(size = 13),
      plot.title         = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      # Left column needs a wide left margin for species name annotations (placed at
      # x = 5.5 m, outside the panel which starts at 7 m). 70 pt gives ~55 pt of
      # space between x = 5.5 m and the figure boundary. Increase further if clipped.
      plot.margin        = if (show_y_labels) margin(5, 8, 5, 70, "pt")
                           else margin(5, 8, 5, 5, "pt")
    )

  # ── Species name labels (all panels) ──
  # Placed at x = 4.0 m, within x_lims[1] = 3.5 m so scale_x_log10 does not drop it.
  # Centred vertically at each species group midpoint (Elk: 1.5, Cattle: 3.5, Horse: 7.5).
  # Appears in every panel; left-column panels have the wider margin but labels render
  # via coord_cartesian(clip = "off") in both columns.
  # If clipped in right column, increase plot.margin right or nudge x toward 6.
  p <- p +
    annotate("text", x = 4.0, y = 1.5, label = "Elk",
             hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 4.0, y = 3.5, label = "Cattle",
             hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 4.0, y = 7.5, label = "Horse",
             hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold")

  p
}

# ── Generate 7 covariate panels ──
# Sort labels alphabetically to match the original facet_wrap ordering
sorted_labels <- sort(covar_labels)

# Layout: 4 rows × 2 cols. Panels 6 (bottom of col 2) and 7 (bottom of col 1)
# need x-axis titles since they sit above the legend / plot edge.
covar_panels <- lapply(seq_along(sorted_labels), function(i) {
  build_domain_panel(
    cv_label      = sorted_labels[i],
    show_x_title  = i >= 6,         # panels 6 and 7 get x-axis titles
    show_y_labels = (i %% 2 == 1)   # odd = left column → show y labels
  )
})

# ── Legend panel (position 8 — the empty slot in the 4×2 grid) ──
# Content is shifted +0.5 units right (all x = 0 → 0.5, x = 1.9 → 2.4, etc.)
# relative to the original to better centre within the panel column.
# Adjust x positions and xlim together if panel width changes.
legend_plot <- ggplot() +
  # --- Domain sign ---
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 10, label = "Domain sign (95% CI)",
           fontface = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 4.5) +
  annotate("segment", x = 0.5, xend = 2.0, y = 9.3, yend = 9.3,
           colour = pos_col, linewidth = 4.5, lineend = "round") +
  annotate("text", x = 2.4, y = 9.3, label = "Positive", hjust = 0, size = 3.8) +
  annotate("segment", x = 0.5, xend = 2.0, y = 8.6, yend = 8.6,
           colour = neg_col, linewidth = 4.5, lineend = "round") +
  annotate("text", x = 2.4, y = 8.6, label = "Negative", hjust = 0, size = 3.8) +
  annotate("segment", x = 0.5, xend = 2.0, y = 7.9, yend = 7.9,
           colour = "grey85", linewidth = 4.5, lineend = "round") +
  annotate("text", x = 2.4, y = 7.9, label = "Zero (CI spans zero)",
           hjust = 0, size = 3.8) +
  # --- Peak markers ---
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 7.0, label = "Peak markers",
           fontface = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 4.5) +
  # Two diamonds side-by-side: filled with domain colour, black outline — matches plot markers
  annotate("point", x = 1.05, y = 6.35, shape = 23, size = 4.5,
           fill = pos_col, colour = "black", stroke = 0.9) +
  annotate("point", x = 1.45, y = 6.35, shape = 23, size = 4.5,
           fill = neg_col, colour = "black", stroke = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = 2.4, y = 6.35, label = "Peak within domain (+/\u2212)",
           hjust = 0, size = 3.8) +
  # Stars use geom_star() so fill + border render correctly (annotate lacks geom_star support)
  geom_star(data = tibble(x = c(1.05, 1.45), y = 5.7,
                          fill = c(pos_col, neg_col)),
            aes(x = x, y = y, fill = fill),
            starshape = 1, colour = "black", starstroke = 0.9, size = 4.0,
            inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  annotate("text", x = 2.4, y = 5.7,
           label = "Global peak (largest |\u03B2|)",
           hjust = 0, size = 3.8) +
  # --- Bracket ---
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 4.8, label = "Cross Domain CI Overlap with Peak",
           fontface = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 4.5) +
  # Blue bracket example (positive domains)
  annotate("segment", x = 0.65, xend = 1.85, y = 4.15, yend = 4.15,
           linewidth = 0.9, colour = pos_col) +
  annotate("segment", x = 0.65, xend = 0.65, y = 3.95, yend = 4.15,
           linewidth = 0.9, colour = pos_col) +
  annotate("segment", x = 1.85, xend = 1.85, y = 3.95, yend = 4.15,
           linewidth = 0.9, colour = pos_col) +
  # Vermillion bracket example (negative domains)
  annotate("segment", x = 0.65, xend = 1.85, y = 3.45, yend = 3.45,
           linewidth = 0.9, colour = neg_col) +
  annotate("segment", x = 0.65, xend = 0.65, y = 3.25, yend = 3.45,
           linewidth = 0.9, colour = neg_col) +
  annotate("segment", x = 1.85, xend = 1.85, y = 3.25, yend = 3.45,
           linewidth = 0.9, colour = neg_col) +
  annotate("text", x = 2.4, y = 3.75,
           label = "Split-domain peaks with\noverlapping 95% CIs",
           hjust = 0, size = 3.8, lineheight = 0.9) +
  xlim(-0.3, 7) + ylim(2.5, 10.5) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(20, 10, 10, 20, "pt"))

# ── Assemble with patchwork ──
domain_fig <- wrap_plots(c(covar_panels, list(legend_plot)), ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Scale of Effect Profiles and Domains of Scale",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold")
    )
  )

domain_fig
```

## Univariate domain classification and visualization (SI)

Parallel domain classification and visualization applied to the univariate
model output. Purpose: sensitivity check on the multivariate domain
structure — comparing univariate and multivariate peaks/domains reveals
whether the scale-of-effect patterns reported above are driven by the
specific covariate combinations in the base/substitution models, or
whether they emerge from the marginal covariate–response relationships
regardless of multivariate conditioning.

Unlike the multivariate analysis, which pools cattle bimonthly and elk
quarterly to meet each species' covariate budget, the univariate fits
operate at monthly resolution for all three species. Because univariate
models estimate only one habitat covariate at a time, there is no
events-per-predictor constraint that would require temporal pooling.
This expands the temporal grid from 10 species × period cells
(multivariate) to 16 cells (univariate): horse 6 months (May–Oct),
cattle 4 months (Jul–Oct; May and June excluded from the univariate
grid), and elk 6 months
(May–Oct). Direct like-for-like comparison with the multivariate domain
plot is therefore only possible for horses, whose temporal pooling
structure is identical across the two analyses.

### Univariate domain tables

```{r univar-domain-classification}
# ── 1. Classify each scale into a domain sign (univariate models only) ──
# Uses covar_source == "univariate" from plot_data_clean, which by
# construction (see the Results Assembly chunk) includes both the regular
# univariate fits (single non-NDVI covariate + SAC + strata random intercept)
# and the bivariate NDVI fits (NDVI_herb + p_herb, NDVI_herb coefficient
# retained only) — both tagged "univariate" during results assembly.
univ_data <- plot_data_clean %>%
  filter(covar_source == "univariate") %>%
  arrange(species, period, covariate, extent_radius_m)

domain_data_uni <- univ_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Domain sign based on 95% CI position relative to zero (same rule as §11.2)
    domain_sign = case_when(
      conf.low > 0  ~ "+",
      conf.high < 0 ~ "-",
      TRUE           ~ "0"
    )
  )

# ── 2. Identify contiguous domains ──
# A new domain starts whenever the sign changes across adjacent scales
# within a species-period-covariate group.
domain_data_uni <- domain_data_uni %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate) %>%
  mutate(
    sign_change = domain_sign != lag(domain_sign, default = first(domain_sign)),
    domain_id = cumsum(sign_change)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r univar-domain-summary}
# ── 3. Summarise each domain (univariate) ──
# Parallel to domain_summary in §11.2; one row per species × period × covariate × domain_id.
domain_summary_uni <- domain_data_uni %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate, domain_id, domain_sign) %>%
  summarise(
    n_scales       = n(),
    scale_min_m    = min(extent_radius_m),
    scale_max_m    = max(extent_radius_m),
    # Peak scale of effect: highest absolute coefficient within domain
    peak_scale_m   = extent_radius_m[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    peak_estimate  = estimate[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    peak_se        = std.error[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    peak_ci_low    = conf.low[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    peak_ci_high   = conf.high[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    peak_p         = p.value[which.max(abs(estimate))],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(species, covariate, period, domain_id)

# ── Table render suppressed in SI ──
# The univariate per-domain table runs to ~150 rows (all three species
# at monthly resolution). The full scale-of-effect structure is shown
# in the univariate domain bar chart (Key figures §1.3 / §11.5). Raw
# per-domain numbers are exported as domain_summary_univariate.csv.
cat(sprintf("Univariate domain summary: %d rows (see domain_summary_univariate.csv for raw values).\n",
            nrow(domain_summary_uni)))
```

```{r univar-peer-summary}
# ── 4. CI-overlapping peer scales (univariate) ──
# Mirrors the peer_summary logic in §11.2: within each non-zero domain,
# identify all buffer scales whose 95% CI overlaps the peak scale's 95% CI.
# Two intervals [a1, b1] and [a2, b2] overlap iff a1 <= b2 AND a2 <= b1.
domain_with_peak_uni <- domain_data_uni %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate, domain_id) %>%
  mutate(
    peak_idx       = which.max(abs(estimate)),
    peak_scale_m   = extent_radius_m[peak_idx],
    peak_ci_low    = conf.low[peak_idx],
    peak_ci_high   = conf.high[peak_idx],
    overlaps_peak  = (conf.low <= peak_ci_high) & (peak_ci_low <= conf.high),
    is_peak        = (extent_radius_m == peak_scale_m)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

peer_summary_uni <- domain_with_peak_uni %>%
  filter(overlaps_peak) %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate, domain_id) %>%
  summarise(
    domain_sign   = first(domain_sign),
    peak_scale_m  = first(peak_scale_m),
    peak_estimate = estimate[is_peak][1],
    n_peers       = sum(!is_peak),
    peer_scales_m = paste(extent_radius_m[!is_peak], collapse = ", "),
    all_scales_m  = paste(extent_radius_m, collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(species, covariate, period)

# ── Table render suppressed in SI ──
# The univariate per-domain peer-scales table runs to ~120 rows. CI-overlap
# of peer scales with the peak scale is visualised as connecting brackets
# in the univariate domain bar chart (Key figures §1.3 / §11.5). Raw list
# of peer scales per domain is exported as domain_peer_scales_univariate.csv.
cat(sprintf("Univariate peer-scale summary: %d domains with one or more CI-overlapping peer scales.\n",
            nrow(peer_summary_uni)))
```

### Univariate domain visualization

Horizontal bars spanning the scale continuum, coloured by domain sign.
Diamonds mark the peak scale of effect within each non-zero domain;
coloured stars (★) mark the global peak; brackets connect peaks of
same-sign split domains with overlapping CIs. Structure parallels the
multivariate bar chart in §11.4, but the y-axis expands from 10
to 16 rows to accommodate monthly resolution for cattle (Jul–Oct) and
elk (May–Oct).

```{r univar-domain-bars, fig.width=14, fig.height=22, cache=FALSE}
# ============================================================================
# Univariate domain bar chart — parallel to the multivariate Figure 2 (§11.4).
# Reuses global objects from §11.4 (domain_pal, horse_img, cow_img, elk_img,
# scale_breaks, scale_break_labels, x_lims, icon_xmin, icon_xmax, legend_plot,
# covar_labels) so the visual style is identical. Only the row ordering,
# separator positions, icon y-anchors, and data objects differ.
# ============================================================================

# ── Y-axis ordering (univariate: 16 rows) ──
# Species order top→bottom: Horse, Cattle, Elk.
# ggplot places the LAST factor level at the top of a discrete y-axis,
# so the species order is reversed (Elk first, Horse last) and within
# each species block periods are listed latest-first (earliest month at top).
species_period_order_uni <- c(
  # Elk (monthly, May–Oct) — rows 1–6 (bottom block)
  "Elk - Oct", "Elk - Sep", "Elk - Aug",
  "Elk - Jul", "Elk - Jun", "Elk - May",
  # Cattle (univariate monthly, Jul–Oct only) — rows 7–10
  "Cattle - Oct", "Cattle - Sep", "Cattle - Aug", "Cattle - Jul",
  # Horse (monthly, May–Oct) — rows 11–16 (top block)
  "Horse - Oct", "Horse - Sep", "Horse - Aug",
  "Horse - Jul", "Horse - Jun", "Horse - May"
)

# Period-only labels (shown in every panel between icons and bars).
# Full month names since all periods are single months.
period_label_data_uni <- tibble(
  row_label   = factor(species_period_order_uni, levels = species_period_order_uni),
  period_text = c("October", "September", "August",
                  "July", "June", "May",
                  "October", "September", "August", "July",
                  "October", "September", "August",
                  "July", "June", "May")
)

# ── Main bar data (one row per domain) ──
# Note: period in domain_summary_uni is a month abbreviation ("May", "Jun", ...).
# paste("Horse", "-", "May") → "Horse - May" matches species_period_order_uni.
bar_data_uni <- domain_summary_uni %>%
  mutate(
    covar_label = covar_labels[as.character(covariate)],
    row_label   = paste(species, "-", as.character(period)),
    row_label   = factor(row_label, levels = species_period_order_uni)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(row_label))   # drops any period not in the univariate grid

# ── Peak classification: regular peaks vs global peak ──
peak_data_uni <- bar_data_uni %>%
  filter(domain_sign != "0") %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate, covar_label) %>%
  mutate(
    n_nz_domains   = n(),
    is_global_peak = abs(peak_estimate) == max(abs(peak_estimate))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

regular_peaks_uni <- peak_data_uni %>% filter(!is_global_peak)
global_peaks_uni  <- peak_data_uni %>% filter(is_global_peak)

# ── Bracket data: connect peaks of same-sign split domains with overlapping CIs ──
bracket_data_uni <- peak_data_uni %>%
  filter(domain_sign != "0") %>%
  group_by(species, period, covariate, covar_label, domain_sign) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%                        # must have 2+ same-sign domains
  arrange(peak_scale_m, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  reframe({
    pairs <- combn(seq_len(n()), 2, simplify = FALSE)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs, function(idx) {
      i <- idx[1]; j <- idx[2]
      ci_overlap <- peak_ci_low[i] <= peak_ci_high[j] &
                    peak_ci_low[j] <= peak_ci_high[i]
      if (ci_overlap) {
        tibble(
          row_label = row_label[i],
          x_start   = peak_scale_m[i],
          x_end     = peak_scale_m[j],
          bracket_sign = domain_sign[i]
        )
      } else {
        tibble()
      }
    }))
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    y_num       = as.numeric(row_label),
    y_base      = y_num + 0.35,
    bracket_col = ifelse(bracket_sign == "+", "#0072B2", "#B22222")
  )

# ── Species separator positions (univariate grid) ──
# Between Elk (rows 1–6) and Cattle (rows 7–10): 6.5
# Between Cattle (rows 7–10) and Horse (rows 11–16): 10.5
sep_positions_uni <- c(6.5, 10.5)

# ── Panel builder (univariate) ──
# Mirrors build_domain_panel() from §11.4 but points to the _uni data objects
# and uses the expanded species-group row midpoints for icon/annotation anchors:
#   Elk rows    1–6   → centre 3.5  → icon ymin 2.5,  ymax 4.5
#   Cattle rows 7–10  → centre 8.5  → icon ymin 7.8,  ymax 9.2
#   Horse rows 11–16  → centre 13.5 → icon ymin 12.5, ymax 14.5
build_domain_panel_uni <- function(cv_label,
                                   show_x_title  = FALSE,
                                   show_y_labels = TRUE) {
  d      <- bar_data_uni      %>% filter(covar_label == cv_label)
  rp     <- regular_peaks_uni %>% filter(covar_label == cv_label)
  gp     <- global_peaks_uni  %>% filter(covar_label == cv_label)
  br     <- bracket_data_uni  %>% filter(covar_label == cv_label)
  br_pos <- br %>% filter(bracket_sign == "+")
  br_neg <- br %>% filter(bracket_sign == "-")

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(y = row_label)) +
    # ── Species separator lines ──
    geom_hline(yintercept = sep_positions_uni, linetype = "solid",
               colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
    # ── Domain-span bars ──
    geom_segment(aes(x = scale_min_m, xend = scale_max_m,
                     yend = row_label, colour = domain_sign),
                 linewidth = 4, lineend = "round") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = domain_pal, guide = "none") +
    # ── Regular peak markers (filled diamond, domain-sign fill, black outline) ──
    geom_point(data = rp, aes(x = peak_scale_m, fill = domain_sign),
               shape = 23, size = 3.2, colour = "black", stroke = 0.9) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = domain_pal, guide = "none") +
    # ── Global peak markers (ggstar star, domain-sign fill) ──
    geom_star(data = gp, aes(x = peak_scale_m, y = row_label, fill = domain_sign),
              starshape = 1, colour = "black", starstroke = 0.9, size = 4.0,
              inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    # ── Brackets: same-sign split-domain peaks with overlapping CIs (positive) ──
    {if (nrow(br_pos) > 0)
      list(
        geom_segment(data = br_pos, aes(x = x_start, xend = x_end,
                     y = y_base, yend = y_base),
                     linewidth = 0.9, colour = "#0072B2",
                     lineend = "butt", inherit.aes = FALSE),
        geom_segment(data = br_pos, aes(x = x_start, xend = x_start,
                     y = y_num + 0.18, yend = y_base),
                     linewidth = 0.9, colour = "#0072B2",
                     inherit.aes = FALSE),
        geom_segment(data = br_pos, aes(x = x_end, xend = x_end,
                     y = y_num + 0.18, yend = y_base),
                     linewidth = 0.9, colour = "#0072B2",
                     inherit.aes = FALSE)
      )
    else NULL} +
    # ── Brackets (negative) ──
    {if (nrow(br_neg) > 0)
      list(
        geom_segment(data = br_neg, aes(x = x_start, xend = x_end,
                     y = y_base, yend = y_base),
                     linewidth = 0.9, colour = "#B22222",
                     lineend = "butt", inherit.aes = FALSE),
        geom_segment(data = br_neg, aes(x = x_start, xend = x_start,
                     y = y_num + 0.18, yend = y_base),
                     linewidth = 0.9, colour = "#B22222",
                     inherit.aes = FALSE),
        geom_segment(data = br_neg, aes(x = x_end, xend = x_end,
                     y = y_num + 0.18, yend = y_base),
                     linewidth = 0.9, colour = "#B22222",
                     inherit.aes = FALSE)
      )
    else NULL} +
    # ── Period labels (between icons and bars; anchored x = 30 m, right-justified) ──
    geom_text(data = period_label_data_uni,
              aes(x = 30, y = row_label, label = period_text),
              hjust = 1, size = 3.0, colour = "black",
              inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    # ── Animal silhouette icons (reused from §11.4 — already tinted and transparent) ──
    # Elk now bottom (rows 1–6), Horse now top (rows 11–16); Cattle unchanged.
    annotation_custom(
      grob = rasterGrob(elk_img, interpolate = TRUE),
      xmin = icon_xmin, xmax = icon_xmax, ymin = 2.5, ymax = 4.5
    ) +
    annotation_custom(
      grob = rasterGrob(cow_img, interpolate = TRUE),
      xmin = icon_xmin, xmax = icon_xmax, ymin = 7.8, ymax = 9.2
    ) +
    annotation_custom(
      grob = rasterGrob(horse_img, interpolate = TRUE),
      xmin = icon_xmin, xmax = icon_xmax, ymin = 12.5, ymax = 14.5
    ) +
    # ── Axes and scales ──
    scale_x_log10(
      breaks = scale_breaks,
      labels = scale_break_labels,
      limits = x_lims
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(
      title = cv_label,
      x     = if (show_x_title) "Spatial extent (buffer radius)" else NULL,
      y     = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
      axis.text.y        = element_blank(),
      axis.title         = element_text(size = 13),
      plot.title         = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      plot.margin        = if (show_y_labels) margin(5, 8, 5, 70, "pt")
                           else margin(5, 8, 5, 5, "pt")
    )

  # ── Species name labels (repositioned to the univariate row midpoints) ──
  # Elk now at the bottom band centre (3.5), Horse now at the top band centre (13.5).
  p <- p +
    annotate("text", x = 4.0, y = 3.5,  label = "Elk",
             hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 4.0, y = 8.5,  label = "Cattle",
             hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 4.0, y = 13.5, label = "Horse",
             hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold")

  p
}

# ── Generate 7 covariate panels (univariate) ──
sorted_labels <- sort(covar_labels)

covar_panels_uni <- lapply(seq_along(sorted_labels), function(i) {
  build_domain_panel_uni(
    cv_label      = sorted_labels[i],
    show_x_title  = i >= 6,            # panels 6 and 7 get x-axis titles
    show_y_labels = (i %% 2 == 1)      # odd = left column → wider left margin
  )
})

# ── Legend panel: reuse legend_plot from §11.4 (not species- or period-specific) ──
# If §11.4 has not been run in the current session, legend_plot will not exist;
# in that case knit from the top or run the domain-bars chunk in §11.4 first.

# ── Assemble with patchwork ──
domain_fig_uni <- wrap_plots(c(covar_panels_uni, list(legend_plot)), ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Scale of Effect Profiles and Domains of Scale — univariate models (SI)",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold")
    )
  )

domain_fig_uni
```

## Univariate–multivariate agreement (Horse)

Quantifies how closely the univariate domain structure reproduces the
multivariate domain structure for horses — the only species with an
identical temporal grid in both analyses (monthly, May–Oct). Cattle and
elk cannot be directly compared because their multivariate models pool
bimonthly and quarterly, respectively, while their univariate models
fit monthly. Horse yields 6 months × 7 covariates = 42 profile-level
comparisons and 6 × 7 × 16 = 672 scale-level comparisons.

**Interpretation.** High agreement on horse profiles increases
confidence that the univariate results for cattle and elk — which are
not directly comparable at the multivariate temporal resolution —
carry similar information about scale structure. Low agreement would
indicate that multivariate conditioning is load-bearing, and the
univariate sensitivity check cannot be read as a stand-alone inference
tool for the finer-grained temporal patterns.

**Caveat on NDVI_herb.** The "univariate" NDVI_herb fits are actually
bivariate (NDVI_herb + p_herb + SAC + strata), because p_herb must be
retained whenever NDVI_herb is in the model to make imputed zeros
interpretable (see NDVI imputation rationale in Methods). The comparison
for NDVI_herb is therefore bivariate-vs-multivariate, not true
univariate-vs-multivariate. Included here because the intent —
isolating NDVI_herb from the full base covariate set — is analogous.

**Terminology used in the tables below.** *Detect* = the model
produced ≥ 1 non-zero domain for that profile (≥ 1 buffer whose 95 %
CI excluded zero in a consistent direction). *Sign reproduction* = the
UNI global peak has the same sign as the MV global peak. *Within-
domain peak agreement* is MV-anchored: for each MV non-zero domain, we
locate the same-sign UNI domain in the same profile with the closest
peak on the log-spaced buffer grid, then ask whether their peak scales
coincide (exactly, or within ±1 buffer class).

```{r profile-global-helper}
# ── Helper: collapse a domain_summary to one row per profile ──
# Each (species, period, covariate) profile is reduced to a "global peak":
# the row with the largest |peak_estimate| across its non-zero domains.
# Profiles with no non-zero domain are kept with NA scale/estimate and
# gp_domain_sign = "0" so they can be counted as null matches.
profile_global <- function(ds) {
  # Count non-zero domains per profile (attached back at the end)
  nz_counts <- ds %>%
    group_by(species, period, covariate) %>%
    summarise(n_domains_nz = sum(domain_sign != "0"), .groups = "drop")

  # Sort within profile so the first row is the global peak
  # (max |peak_estimate| among non-zero domains, NA sorted last)
  ds %>%
    mutate(
      is_nz   = domain_sign != "0",
      abs_est = ifelse(is_nz, abs(peak_estimate), NA_real_)
    ) %>%
    arrange(species, period, covariate, desc(abs_est)) %>%
    group_by(species, period, covariate) %>%
    slice(1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      gp_domain_sign   = domain_sign,
      gp_peak_scale_m  = ifelse(is_nz, peak_scale_m,  NA_real_),
      gp_peak_estimate = ifelse(is_nz, peak_estimate, NA_real_),
      gp_peak_ci_low   = ifelse(is_nz, peak_ci_low,   NA_real_),
      gp_peak_ci_high  = ifelse(is_nz, peak_ci_high,  NA_real_)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(species, period, covariate,
                  gp_domain_sign, gp_peak_scale_m, gp_peak_estimate,
                  gp_peak_ci_low, gp_peak_ci_high) %>%
    left_join(nz_counts, by = c("species", "period", "covariate"))
}
```

```{r horse-profile-compare}
# ── Profile-level comparison (Horse only) ──
# Collapse MV and UNI domain summaries to one row per profile, restrict
# to Horse, and join on species × period × covariate.
mv_profiles_horse  <- profile_global(domain_summary)      %>% filter(species == "Horse")
uni_profiles_horse <- profile_global(domain_summary_uni)  %>% filter(species == "Horse")

horse_compare <- inner_join(
  mv_profiles_horse,
  uni_profiles_horse,
  by = c("species", "period", "covariate"),
  suffix = c("_mv", "_uni")
) %>%
  mutate(
    # Detect-status partition (null / both / MV-only / UNI-only)
    both_detect = (gp_domain_sign_mv != "0") & (gp_domain_sign_uni != "0"),
    only_mv     = (gp_domain_sign_mv != "0") & (gp_domain_sign_uni == "0"),
    only_uni    = (gp_domain_sign_mv == "0") & (gp_domain_sign_uni != "0"),

    # Sign agreement at the global peak (defined only when both detect)
    sign_match  = ifelse(both_detect,
                         gp_domain_sign_mv == gp_domain_sign_uni, NA),

    # Peak-scale distance on the log-spaced buffer grid: "±1 class" is the
    # meaningful resolution unit given log-spaced sampling; raw metres
    # would understate agreement at fine scales and overstate it at broad.
    peak_idx_mv      = match(gp_peak_scale_m_mv,  scale_breaks),
    peak_idx_uni     = match(gp_peak_scale_m_uni, scale_breaks),
    peak_within_1    = abs(peak_idx_mv - peak_idx_uni) <= 1,

    # CI overlap at respective peak scales on the log-rate scale
    # Intervals [a1,b1], [a2,b2] overlap iff a1 <= b2 AND a2 <= b1.
    ci_overlap_at_peak = ifelse(
      both_detect,
      (gp_peak_ci_low_mv  <= gp_peak_ci_high_uni) &
      (gp_peak_ci_low_uni <= gp_peak_ci_high_mv),
      NA
    )
  )
```

```{r horse-within-domain-match}
# ── Within-MV-domain peak-scale matching (Horse only) ──
# For each of the 45 MV non-zero domains, locate the same-sign UNI
# domain in the same profile with the closest peak on the log-spaced
# buffer grid, then test whether their peak scales coincide exactly
# or within ±1 buffer class. This answers the per-domain (rather than
# per-profile) scale-of-effect agreement question underlying the
# Results sentence:
#
#   "UV scale of effect within each of the 45 domains that MV models
#    also detected agreed x% of the time (X% ±1 buffer)."
#
# Denominator = 45 MV non-zero domains (all MV non-zero domains count
# against agreement, including the four MV-only profiles that have no
# same-sign UNI counterpart and the one Sep p_wetland profile where
# MV and UNI disagree in sign at the global peak). Reuse of a single
# UNI domain as the best match for multiple MV domains is permitted —
# the question is whether UNI could reproduce each MV peak, not a
# one-to-one assignment.

mv_nz_horse <- domain_summary %>%
  filter(species == "Horse", domain_sign != "0") %>%
  # Index within (profile × sign) so rows are preserved when a profile
  # contains multiple same-sign domains
  group_by(species, period, covariate, domain_sign) %>%
  mutate(mv_dom_id = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, covariate, domain_sign, mv_dom_id,
                mv_peak_scale_m  = peak_scale_m,
                mv_peak_estimate = peak_estimate)

uni_nz_horse <- domain_summary_uni %>%
  filter(species == "Horse", domain_sign != "0") %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, covariate, domain_sign,
                uni_peak_scale_m  = peak_scale_m,
                uni_peak_estimate = peak_estimate)

mv_domain_match <- mv_nz_horse %>%
  left_join(uni_nz_horse,
            by = c("species", "period", "covariate", "domain_sign"),
            relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  mutate(
    mv_peak_idx  = match(mv_peak_scale_m,  scale_breaks),
    uni_peak_idx = match(uni_peak_scale_m, scale_breaks),
    idx_dist     = abs(mv_peak_idx - uni_peak_idx)
  ) %>%
  # Best UNI match per MV domain (smallest idx_dist; NA sorts last,
  # so MV domains with no same-sign UNI counterpart keep their NA row)
  group_by(species, period, covariate, domain_sign, mv_dom_id,
           mv_peak_scale_m) %>%
  arrange(idx_dist, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    uni_matched   = !is.na(uni_peak_scale_m),
    peak_exact    = uni_matched & idx_dist == 0,
    peak_within_1 = uni_matched & idx_dist <= 1
  )

# Sanity check: number of rows should equal total MV non-zero domains
stopifnot(nrow(mv_domain_match) == sum(horse_compare$n_domains_nz_mv))

n_mv_domains     <- nrow(mv_domain_match)                        # expect 45
n_mv_matched_uni <- sum(mv_domain_match$uni_matched)
n_peak_exact_dom <- sum(mv_domain_match$peak_exact)
n_peak_w1_dom    <- sum(mv_domain_match$peak_within_1)
```

```{r horse-scale-level-compare}
# ── Scale-level sign classification (672 cells = 6 × 7 × 16) ──
# Key finding: does the cell-level sign contingency include any
# +/− or −/+ pairs (true directional disagreement)? Anything else
# reduces to detection-threshold differences, which are captured by
# the profile-level 'MV only' / 'UNI only' rows in the summary table.
horse_scale_compare <- inner_join(
  domain_data %>%
    filter(species == "Horse") %>%
    dplyr::select(species, period, covariate, extent_radius_m, domain_sign),
  domain_data_uni %>%
    filter(species == "Horse") %>%
    dplyr::select(species, period, covariate, extent_radius_m, domain_sign),
  by = c("species", "period", "covariate", "extent_radius_m"),
  suffix = c("_mv", "_uni")
)

sign_pair_tab <- horse_scale_compare %>%
  count(domain_sign_mv, domain_sign_uni) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

knitr::kable(
  sign_pair_tab,
  caption = sprintf(
    "Horse: cell-level sign classification, %d cells. Any +/− or −/+ row would indicate a true directional disagreement between analyses.",
    nrow(horse_scale_compare)
  ),
  col.names = c("Sign (MV)", "Sign (UNI)", "N cells", "%")
)
```

```{r horse-profile-summary-table}
# ── Consolidated Horse agreement metrics ──
# Rolls four levels of resolution into one table:
#   (1) Profile-level detect counts (denominator = 42 profiles)
#   (2) Global-peak agreement metrics (denominator varies: 30 MV-detect
#       for sign reproduction; 26 both-detect for sign-match, peak, CI)
#   (3) MV-anchored within-domain peak agreement (denominator = 45 MV
#       non-zero domains)
#   (4) Cell-level sign agreement (denominator = 672 buffer cells)
# Detect = ≥ 1 non-zero domain for that profile.

n_profiles   <- nrow(horse_compare)
n_mv_detect  <- sum(horse_compare$gp_domain_sign_mv  != "0")
n_uni_detect <- sum(horse_compare$gp_domain_sign_uni != "0")
n_both       <- sum(horse_compare$both_detect)
n_mv_signrep <- sum(horse_compare$gp_domain_sign_mv != "0" &
                    horse_compare$gp_domain_sign_mv ==
                      horse_compare$gp_domain_sign_uni)
n_mv_domains_tot  <- sum(horse_compare$n_domains_nz_mv)
n_uni_domains_tot <- sum(horse_compare$n_domains_nz_uni)
n_cells           <- nrow(horse_scale_compare)
n_cell_match      <- sum(horse_scale_compare$domain_sign_mv ==
                         horse_scale_compare$domain_sign_uni)
n_cell_reverse    <- sum(
  (horse_scale_compare$domain_sign_mv == "+" &
   horse_scale_compare$domain_sign_uni == "-") |
  (horse_scale_compare$domain_sign_mv == "-" &
   horse_scale_compare$domain_sign_uni == "+")
)
n_global_exact    <- sum(horse_compare$peak_idx_mv ==
                         horse_compare$peak_idx_uni, na.rm = TRUE)

horse_summary_stats <- tibble(
  metric = c(
    # Profile-level detect counts
    "Profiles compared (Horse, 6 months × 7 covariates)",
    "Profiles with ≥ 1 MV non-zero domain ('MV detects')",
    "Profiles with ≥ 1 UNI non-zero domain ('UNI detects')",
    "Profiles with ≥ 1 non-zero domain in both analyses",
    "Profiles detected only in multivariate (MV only)",
    "Profiles detected only in univariate (UNI only)",
    # Global-peak agreement
    "MV sign reproduced by UNI at global peak | MV detects",
    "Sign agreement at global peak | both detect",
    "Global peak exact match on buffer grid | both detect",
    "Global peak within ±1 buffer class | both detect",
    "CI overlap at peak scales | both detect",
    # Domain counts
    "MV non-zero domains (total across 42 profiles)",
    "UNI non-zero domains (total across 42 profiles)",
    # Within-domain peak (MV-anchored)
    "Within-domain peak: exact match | MV-anchored (of 45 MV domains)",
    "Within-domain peak: within ±1 buffer class | MV-anchored",
    # Cell-level
    "Cell-level sign agreement (same sign incl. 0/0) | 672 cells",
    "Cell-level sign reversals (+/− or −/+) | 672 cells"
  ),
  N = c(
    n_profiles,
    n_mv_detect,
    n_uni_detect,
    n_both,
    sum(horse_compare$only_mv),
    sum(horse_compare$only_uni),
    n_mv_signrep,
    sum(horse_compare$sign_match,         na.rm = TRUE),
    n_global_exact,
    sum(horse_compare$peak_within_1,      na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(horse_compare$ci_overlap_at_peak, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_mv_domains_tot,
    n_uni_domains_tot,
    n_peak_exact_dom,
    n_peak_w1_dom,
    n_cell_match,
    n_cell_reverse
  ),
  denominator = c(
    n_profiles, n_profiles, n_profiles, n_profiles, n_profiles, n_profiles,
    n_mv_detect,
    n_both, n_both, n_both, n_both,
    NA_integer_, NA_integer_,
    n_mv_domains_tot, n_mv_domains_tot,
    n_cells, n_cells
  )
) %>%
  mutate(percentage = ifelse(!is.na(denominator),
                             round(100 * N / denominator, 1),
                             NA_real_))

knitr::kable(
  horse_summary_stats,
  caption = sprintf(
    "Horse: agreement between multivariate and univariate scale-of-effect structure, resolved at the profile, domain, and buffer-cell levels. 'Detect' = ≥ 1 non-zero domain. MV-anchored within-domain peak match: for each of the %d MV non-zero domains, the closest same-sign UNI domain in that profile on the log-spaced buffer grid (see preceding chunk for logic).",
    n_mv_domains_tot
  ),
  col.names = c("Agreement criterion", "N", "Denominator", "%")
)
```

### Decomposing the disagreements

A covariate-level decomposition of the cell-level contingency shows
how the detection-threshold asymmetries are distributed across the
seven covariates. The per-covariate buckets below collapse the full
9-cell (MV × UNI) contingency to five mutually exclusive categories
so the breakdown fits on one page; a "Sign reversal" column would
appear only if any +/− or −/+ cell existed (none do).

```{r per-covariate-disagreement}
# ── Per-covariate cell-level sign pairs ──
# Collapses the 9-cell (MV × UNI) contingency into five mutually
# exclusive buckets per covariate so that the per-covariate breakdown
# fits on one page. "Sign reversal" = true +/- or -/+ directional
# disagreement (expected to be 0 throughout — included as a visible check).
per_covar_disagreement <- horse_scale_compare %>%
  mutate(
    bucket = case_when(
      domain_sign_mv == domain_sign_uni                ~ "Match (any sign)",
      domain_sign_mv == "0"  & domain_sign_uni == "+"  ~ "MV=0, UNI=+",
      domain_sign_mv == "0"  & domain_sign_uni == "-"  ~ "MV=0, UNI=-",
      domain_sign_mv == "+"  & domain_sign_uni == "0"  ~ "MV=+, UNI=0",
      domain_sign_mv == "-"  & domain_sign_uni == "0"  ~ "MV=-, UNI=0",
      TRUE                                              ~ "Sign reversal"
    )
  ) %>%
  count(covariate, bucket) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = bucket, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  dplyr::select(covariate,
                `Match (any sign)`,
                `MV=0, UNI=+`, `MV=0, UNI=-`,
                `MV=+, UNI=0`, `MV=-, UNI=0`,
                any_of("Sign reversal")) %>%
  arrange(covariate)

knitr::kable(
  per_covar_disagreement,
  caption = "Horse: per-covariate cell-level disagreement structure (cells out of 96 per covariate: 6 months × 16 buffers). Shows whether the UNI→+ excess is concentrated in particular covariates or distributed across them."
)
```
